item.title: French policemen go on trial over 2020 beating of Black music producer
item.description: Three French policemen went on trial on Monday, November 9, over the beating of a Black music producer they say was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic, in a rare police brutality case to go to court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic.

item.title: TNA Wrestler suffers serious car accident
item.description: TNA Wrestler suffers serious car accident appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . TNA wrestler Jada Stone recently suffered a serious car accident. Shortly after the accident , Stone shared on social media that she was “blessed to be alive.” Stone shared an update on her Instagram Story on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, saying the car accident had occurred two nights earlier. “Two nights ago, I was in a pretty bad wreck. I’m okay…car unfortunately is not! I’m so blessed to be alive! Be safe on the road everyone!,” she wrote. Stone shared pictures of herself showing bruising on her face, wearing a neck brace, and sporting a large bandage wrapped around one of her legs. She also attached a picture of her wrecked car. Stone added that she had already contacted promoters regarding canceling future bookings. Stone did not disclose any specific injuries or share any additional details on how the accident occurred. Stone also wrestles under the nickname “The Spark.” She made her professional debut in 2021 and later signed with TNA in 2025. Recently, she became a more regular presence on TNA programming earlier this year, 2026, recording a television win against Tasha Steelz in February. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Her most memorable run to date came earlier this year in the TNA Knockouts Television Championship tournament. In the tournament, Stone defeated Alisha Edwards, Jody Threat and Heather By Elegance before reaching the tournament final against M By Elegance on Aug. 27, 2026. However, she lost to M By Elegance in the tournament final. Later, she received another title opportunity in the Oct. 29, 2026 episode of TNA Impact, where she again lost. Stone has also wrestled on the independent scene and has competed in Japan and Mexico. TNA wrestler Jada Stone revealed on IG Stories that she was in a car accident. 🙏 pic.twitter.com/uZIauZNBOv — Fightful Wrestling (@Fightful) November 8, 2026 Related: Taylor Swift reunites with Karlie Kloss at Chiefs game after rumored feud Related: Former ESPN star calls out NFL WAGs Brittany Mahomes, Kelly Stafford over recent comments

item.title: Olympic Judo Champion Riner Joins Fight For French Presidency
item.description: France’s five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in the country’s high-stakes presidential election next year. “My name is Teddy Riner and today, I am telling you face to face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election,” the 37-year-old said in a surprise announcement on social media. Riner, among France’s best-known sports figures, enters the race with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen leading in the polls to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron next year. France’s Teddy Riner (Blue) reacts after beating South Korea’s Kim Min-jong in the judo men’s +100kg gold bout of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games at the Champ-de-Mars Arena, in Paris on August 2, 2024. He has publicly said he was very worried about the “rise of the far right” in France. Riner has won five Olympic gold medals in judo. He won the heavyweight division at the 2012, 2016 and 2024 Olympics and mixed team golds at the 2020 and 2024 Games. Riner has also won 11 world titles. Another French star judoka, David Douillet, was elected to the French parliament in 2009 and served as sports minister from September 2011 to May 2012. AFP The post Olympic Judo Champion Riner Joins Fight For French Presidency appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Barcelona superstar to miss Spain’s Czech Republic match after suffering knee discomfort against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Barcelona superstar to miss Spain’s Czech Republic match after suffering knee discomfort against Atletico Madrid Barcelona have been handed a fitness concern after Lamine Yamal reported discomfort in his right knee following their 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid . As a result, according to Mundo Deportivo , the forward will remain in Barcelona rather than travel with Spain for Thursday’s Nations League fixture against the Czech Republic, with his availability for the meeting with England on November 15 still dependent on his recovery. The outlet mentions that Yamal underwent medical tests after Sunday’s match at the Metropolitano, and the decision was taken for him to continue his recovery in Barcelona. Indeed, the Spanish international is expected to join Luis de la Fuente’s squad in the coming days, but his participation against England cannot yet be considered certain. Yamal to miss Spain’s trip to face Czech Republic Spain are scheduled to face the Czech Republic in Prague on November 12 before hosting England at the Metropolitano three days later. Lamine Yamal suffered knee discomfort vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yamal is expected to miss the first fixture as Barcelona and the national team’s medical staff monitor his condition. The forward was the only Barcelona international to return to the club immediately after the victory over Atletico, while his teammates remained in Madrid ahead of their international commitments. For now, the Royal Spanish Football Federation’s medical department is maintaining contact with Barcelona’s doctors to follow the progress of the affected players. Understandably, the priority will be to assess the 19-year-old’s recovery before deciding whether he can join the national team group and feature in the second fixture. Flick faces another concern over Yamal’s workload The situation is an unwelcome development for Hansi Flick, particularly after Yamal played an important role in Barcelona’s victory against Atletico. Lamine Yamal will miss Spain’s next match vs Czech Republic. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The teenager provided the assist for Fermin Lopez’s decisive goal in the 66th minute, helping the Catalans secure three valuable points. Flick had already highlighted the difficulty of managing players’ workloads during international breaks , with several Barcelona regulars leaving to represent their countries. “It’s part of our job: there’s an international break now, and the Spanish players are usually not here during those breaks. “Managing playing time is crucial. It’s important that they do the same with their national teams,” he noted. As a result of the aforementioned development, the immediate concern will be to ensure that Yamal does not aggravate the discomfort while travelling or returning to competitive action too soon, something that Barcelona learned the hard way through Raphinha’s recent problems.

item.title: Nasarawa vows peaceful polls, warns against electoral violence
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to conducting free, fair, transparent and peaceful elections, warning individuals and groups planning to instigate violence that they will be arrested and prosecuted. The State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, gave the assurance while addressing journalists, stakeholders, party supporters and government partners in Lafia on Monday. Aboki said the government was monitoring the security situation across the state’s local government areas to ensure that voters could exercise their franchise without fear or intimidation. Warning those contemplating violence, the commissioner said the government’s preference for peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Quietness does not mean that somebody is weak. At times, when someone is pushed, the time comes when they must act. “Anyone who wants to perpetuate violence will be arrested and prosecuted to ensure we have peaceful elections,” he warned. He urged political parties and candidates to conduct their campaigns in an orderly and civilised manner, stressing that political violence would serve no useful purpose in the electoral process or the development of the state. On voter participation, Aboki urged eligible residents to ensure their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) were ready and safely kept ahead of the elections. He advised voters against waiting until election day to collect their PVCs and encouraged those yet to register to take advantage of the online voter registration platform. Highlighting infrastructure and social development projects undertaken by the Federal Government and the administration of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the commissioner cited the proposed transformation of the Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa, into a specialised mining university, as well as the Leather Designing and Craft School in Doma. On infrastructure, he listed the ongoing federal government dualisation and expansion of the Nasarawa-Keffi road network and the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe Superhighway among projects expected to improve connectivity. In the health sector, Aboki said the upgrading and expansion of the Dalhatu Araf Specialist Hospital into the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, alongside facilities such as the Federal Eye Centre in Doma, had improved access to healthcare. The commissioner called on residents to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) gubernatorial candidate and other party candidates, arguing that such support would sustain the development initiatives of the Sule administration. “I know all of us are happy with the work Governor Sule has done. And so he has given us somebody we need to support. I want to call on all of us, and indeed the people of Nasarawa State, to support the candidate he has given us,” he said. The commissioner said the Sule administration remained open to dialogue and constructive feedback from citizens and development partners to advance its development objectives. item.title: Injecting Plexiglass? A champion cried foul. Bodybuilding’s response raises more questions
item.description: A former champion at the biggest event in women’s bodybuilding recently rocked the sport with a sensational claim about the physical appearance of current champion Natalia Coelho . Sarah Villegas, a four-time former champion , accused Coelho of getting injected with a Plexiglas substance to build fake “plastic” muscles and win the crown for best physique at Ms. Olympia. “I can't believe I have to explain why plastic muscle implants have no place in a sport founded on building actual muscle through human effort,” Villegas told USA TODAY Sports in an interview. “It's called bodybuilding, not plastic building.” And that’s just the tip of this “plastic” iceberg. To wit: ∎ Coelho didn’t deny the claim when given the chance. ∎ Villegas wasn’t making this up out of thin air. She had received unsolicited “firsthand” information about it from a health professional at a clinic in Brazil where the procedure allegedly was performed. USA TODAY reviewed this information and confirmed with this person they shared it with Villegas. This person did not want to be identified because they feared retaliation. Villegas told USA TODAY Sports this matter is an “existential threat” to bodybuilding. She noted the health risks of such injections and said she didn’t want her sport to become a “competition of who has the best cosmetic surgeon.” ∎ The governing body of the sport has a financial interest in disregarding the controversy and didn’t announce any investigation into it. Nor did it respond to several messages about it from USA TODAY Sports. ∎ Meanwhile, top personalities in the business have blamed Villegas for making it an issue and described her as a sore loser. They have claimed there are no rules against the alleged injections. That includes the “Voice of Bodybuilding” Bob Cicherillo, who hosts the prestigious Olympia competition. “I really don't care what anybody's doing,” Cicherillo said on his podcast . “I don't have any moral or ethical fight here of what anybody is doing. I don't care whether… you got Cheez Whiz or anything else that you're putting in your physique. We only get judged on what goes on that stage.” Former Mr. Olympia says 'This is cheating' Such is the state of pro bodybuilding, the same sport that once produced entertainment icons Arnold Schwarzenegge r and Lou Ferrigno , otherwise known as The Incredible Hulk. It’s also a sport where bodybuilders historically have used steroids and other enhancing drugs to boost their physiques and impress judges who determine the winners based on the muscle in their poses and other factors. So then what’s the big deal if some are now trying to win with artificial Plexiglas muscles? “This is cheating,” said Samir Bannout, the 1983 Mr. Olympia. item.content:encoded: A former champion at the biggest event in women’s bodybuilding recently rocked the sport with a sensational claim about the physical appearance of current champion Natalia Coelho . Sarah Villegas, a four-time former champion , accused Coelho of getting injected with a Plexiglas substance to build fake “plastic” muscles and win the crown for best physique at Ms. Olympia. “I can't believe I have to explain why plastic muscle implants have no place in a sport founded on building actual muscle through human effort,” Villegas told USA TODAY Sports in an interview. “It's called bodybuilding, not plastic building.” And that’s just the tip of this “plastic” iceberg. To wit: ∎ Coelho didn’t deny the claim when given the chance. ∎ Villegas wasn’t making this up out of thin air. She had received unsolicited “firsthand” information about it from a health professional at a clinic in Brazil where the procedure allegedly was performed. USA TODAY reviewed this information and confirmed with this person they shared it with Villegas. This person did not want to be identified because they feared retaliation. Villegas told USA TODAY Sports this matter is an “existential threat” to bodybuilding. She noted the health risks of such injections and said she didn’t want her sport to become a “competition of who has the best cosmetic surgeon.” ∎ The governing body of the sport has a financial interest in disregarding the controversy and didn’t announce any investigation into it. Nor did it respond to several messages about it from USA TODAY Sports. ∎ Meanwhile, top personalities in the business have blamed Villegas for making it an issue and described her as a sore loser. They have claimed there are no rules against the alleged injections. That includes the “Voice of Bodybuilding” Bob Cicherillo, who hosts the prestigious Olympia competition. “I really don't care what anybody's doing,” Cicherillo said on his podcast . “I don't have any moral or ethical fight here of what anybody is doing. I don't care whether… you got Cheez Whiz or anything else that you're putting in your physique. We only get judged on what goes on that stage.” Former Mr. Olympia says 'This is cheating' Such is the state of pro bodybuilding, the same sport that once produced entertainment icons Arnold Schwarzenegge r and Lou Ferrigno , otherwise known as The Incredible Hulk. It’s also a sport where bodybuilders historically have used steroids and other enhancing drugs to boost their physiques and impress judges who determine the winners based on the muscle in their poses and other factors. So then what’s the big deal if some are now trying to win with artificial Plexiglas muscles? “This is cheating,” said Samir Bannout, the 1983 Mr. Olympia. In this case, Coelho is accused of using a form of polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA), also known as Plexiglas, to enhance her appearance before winning the women’s physique crown at the Ms. Olympia competition in 2025, beating Villegas, the runner-up. Coelho then won it again in Las Vegas in late September, while Villegas finished third. Villegas’ coach and husband, Ali Taktak, said the person who provided the information about Coelho’s PMMA injections also identified the clinic and doctor where she allegedly got them in Brazil — Fernando Vitor at the Instituto Lappidare. Current champion Coelho declined to confirm or deny allegation USA TODAY Sports confirmed the person who provided this information to Villegas is a licensed health professional in Brazil and that Coelho appeared at this clinic with Vitor, according to a video on Instagram . Vitor and his clinic have financial ties to the sport’s governing body through Tamer El-Guindy , a promoter of bodybuilding events and producer at the Olympia event. Coelho, who grew up in Brazil, hasn’t denied or confirmed whether she received PMMA injections. Cicherillo asked Coelho about the controversy at a public seminar in September . “If I get into that, I’m not doing any good for the sport,” Coelho said. Coelho didn’t return several messages seeking additional comment. Vitor and El-Guindy also didn’t’ return messages. 'We don't have any rules' against Plexiglas muscles The governing body of the sport is the IFBB Pro League , originally known as the International Federation of Body Builders. The organization and its president Jim Manion also did not return several messages seeking comment by phone and email. Nor did Jake Wood, owner of the Olympia event, the top event in the sport. After Villegas received this information about Coelho last year, Villegas said her coach, Taktak, shared it with league leadership. In response, Villegas said the IFBB Pro League stated it “has no rules prohibiting PMMA plastic muscle implants” and that “no one is asked to submit a resume of what they did to attain their physique before stepping on stage.” This response echoed top personalities in the sport who criticized Villegas for speaking out. Shawn Ray, a 13-time Mr. Olympia finalist, said on a podcast with Cicherillo that Villegas “sounds like a sore loser” after getting beat by Coelho for the crown. He and others said there are no rules against this, and it’s up to the judges to pick a winner based on what they see, much like a beauty pageant. Because of that, they defend Coelho. Cicherillo has called Villegas' allegations "very unprofessional." “We don't have any rules set forth and we don't have any testing procedures,” Cicherillo said on a podcast last yea r after Villegas spoke out against Coelho. “This is anything but a 'natural' federation." Ray agreed. Even if Coelho did use PMMA, "What rule would she be breaking?" Ray asked. "If you can find the rule book, what rule book is she breaking?... So where does Sarah have a foot to stand on?" Cicherillo and Ray didn't return messages seeking comment. View this post on Instagram Brazil recently banned such injections after woman's death Villegas and others say obtaining artificial muscles tramples the spirit of the competition. Instead of building muscle through hard work and nutrition over time, they say PMMA injections skip all of that and render it meaningless. Such injections also can risk disfigurement or worse. In the U.S., the medical use of PMMA is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration only when used as a dermal filler to treat nasolabial folds and acne scars — not to enhance physiques in bodybuilding. In Brazil, PMMA was banned for aesthetic purposes in June shortly after a 48-year-old woman died following a PMMA injection for a cosmetic buttocks augmentation procedure . A government official in Brazil noted the injections could cause “irreversible damage and even death." Substance is designed to 'add volume' for cosmetic reasons in U.S. In the U.S., cosmetic PMMA injections consist of PMMA microspheres in bovine collagen — a product known as Bellafill. California doctor Steven Williams told USA TODAY Sports the idea of using it to enhance muscle artificially "makes some sense" because "a little volume goes a long way" with aesthetic concerns. "After injection, the bovine collagen is absorbed leaving the (PMMA) beads to create more volume," said Williams, a member of the American Society of Plastic Surgeons. "Because it can add volume some people have tried using it to add volume in other parts of the body." Williams told USA TODAY Sports that using it for muscle volume in the U.S. would be considered "off label," which means the FDA hasn't studied its safety for this purpose or legitimized the claimed benefits. In bodybuilding, using PMMA to enhance physiques has been talked about for years with scant public confirmations of actual usage. Many in the business say bodybuilder Rich Piana was known for it before he died in 2017 at age 46 . Longtime bodybuilders who consider it cheating say it's different than using steroids because using steroids still required hard work to build those muscles. That’s not the case with PMMA. item.title: Vikings are dead in the water unless they solve QB problem in next 24 hours | Opinion
item.description: If it seems like the Vikings had an easier time finding North America than the Lombardi Trophy, well, maybe Leif Erikson was a much more effective navigator than Kyler Murray . But, more topically, if the NFC North leaders from Minnesota want to have any shot at finally entering football Valhalla this season, they better figure out their quarterback conundrum − and might only have the next 24 hours or so to do it. Minnesota and the Buffalo Bills entered Week 9 tied (with the San Francisco 49ers) for the NFL's best record at 6-1 and will meet Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. The Bills are built around quarterback Josh Allen, who's trying to win league MVP honors for the second time in three seasons. The Vikings are built like a house of cards, with backup Carson Wentz − one of nine quarterbacks to start for the team during head coach Kevin O'Connell's five-season tenure − set to play for the third time this season in place of Murray, who's nursing a tender hamstring. And while turning to the QB2 is generally suboptimal, particularly for a team battling to be the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff field, Wentz could provide important clarity to a team that boasts perhaps the NFL's most ferocious defense − and certainly its stingiest when it comes to giving up points − but hasn't been able to score much itself, ranking 27th in points per game entering week 9 and 29th overall offensively. item.content:encoded: If it seems like the Vikings had an easier time finding North America than the Lombardi Trophy, well, maybe Leif Erikson was a much more effective navigator than Kyler Murray . But, more topically, if the NFC North leaders from Minnesota want to have any shot at finally entering football Valhalla this season, they better figure out their quarterback conundrum − and might only have the next 24 hours or so to do it. Minnesota and the Buffalo Bills entered Week 9 tied (with the San Francisco 49ers) for the NFL's best record at 6-1 and will meet Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. The Bills are built around quarterback Josh Allen, who's trying to win league MVP honors for the second time in three seasons. The Vikings are built like a house of cards, with backup Carson Wentz − one of nine quarterbacks to start for the team during head coach Kevin O'Connell's five-season tenure − set to play for the third time this season in place of Murray, who's nursing a tender hamstring. And while turning to the QB2 is generally suboptimal, particularly for a team battling to be the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff field, Wentz could provide important clarity to a team that boasts perhaps the NFL's most ferocious defense − and certainly its stingiest when it comes to giving up points − but hasn't been able to score much itself, ranking 27th in points per game entering week 9 and 29th overall offensively. "Kyler Murray, I don't know if he's a great fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense," NFL Network analyst Steve Mariucci, formerly the head coach of the 49ers and Detroit Lions, said last week. "He's a heck of an athlete, he's an improviser and all that. But they want to play from the pocket − play-action pass, throw the ball down the field − I don't know if that's Kyler Murray's deal." It's decidedly not. Murray, the 2018 Heisman Trophy winner and No. 1 overall pick of the 2019 NFL Draft by the Arizona Cardinals, is a two-time Pro Bowler who's historically been known for his live arm and the juice in his legs − though that's often led him to bail from the pocket while trying to make an impromptu play when his first read is covered. But that element of his game has waned as injuries have taken a toll on the 29-year-old, and it's hardly been evident at all as he's struggled to find a groove in O'Connell's attack. Worse, Murray has failed to leverage the Vikings' best player, perennial Pro Bowler Justin Jefferson, who's as talented as any wideout in the league but is averaging fewer than five receptions and 60 receiving yards per game in 2026. "They've got nowhere to go. I don't see Kyler getting better and resurrecting his career. Way too inconsistent, doesn't anticipate well," former New York Giants vice president of player personnel Marc Ross told USA TODAY Sports. "And Kevin O'Connell hasn't really shown any ability to help Murray out to this point." O'Connell, who has a reputation as a quarterback whisperer, bemoaned the lack of offensive execution after last week's 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions, Minnesota's first of the season. He's also noted that the team has been in the shotgun formation a lot more this season, which is Murray's preference, though that's probably come at the expense of running the ball more effectively − and it hasn't helped get Jefferson sufficiently involved, either. "I thought there were some play-pass chances that we didn't see or didn't pull the trigger on," O'Connell said after the loss at Ford Field, when Murray connected five times with Jefferson for just 33 yards, though one hook-up did produce a TD. "We know how much (Jefferson) impacts the game, so it's going to be something we'll continue to emphasize and continue to try to do both in rhythm on the scheduled timing of the play and then some of the off-schedule opportunities as well. "(Murray is) in the gun a lot. We're marrying that up as creatively and as effectively as we can. ... So, I think it's just continuing to build that rapport of the plans, the comfort level, continuing to implore some input from him on things he likes and (saying), ‘Hey, how can we carve it and make it even more cleaner and better for him?’ so that we do get some of that comfort where he'll throw things with anticipation, and we get to look for a play. We all know it's coming." Is Carson Wentz the Vikings' QB answer? But is it coming? Six games into his Minnesota career, Murray's 86.6 passer rating ranked 20th in the NFL and lagged about five points behind the league average. In terms of ESPN's QBR metric, his 44.6 figure ranks 26th. And his 170.3 passing yards per game? The lowest figure of his NFL career. "Kyler just doesn't look as if he any confidence or feel flow," said Ross, now an NFL Network analyst. "The defense is good enough to win the whole damn thing, but they have to hold everyone to 13 points. If they can just get anything from the offense …" A big if, but one the Vikings can now assess freshly with Wentz, who helped lead Minnesota to wins in the first two games of the season after Murray was concussed in the first quarter of the opener. And while O'Connell said last week he remains committed to Murray as his starter, he also spelled out what he expects Wentz to provide against Buffalo. "He’s going to throw a lot of completions. He’s going to put the ball in play. He’s got such a high, high understanding of not only the offense, but what he’s looking at on the other side. He’s got 100 games of experience," O'Connell said of Wentz, the No. 2 pick of the 2016 draft who put the Philadelphia Eagles on the path to their first Super Bowl victory but went down with a knee injury late in the 2017 season. Knowing where his bread is buttered − as well as signaling internal locker room frustration − Wentz admitted he plans to feed Jefferson on Monday. Frequently. "Just get him the rock. I mean, he's as good as I've been around," Wentz said of Jefferson, who's averaging more than 30 yards fewer than his career average of 88.2 receiving yards per game, the second-highest figure in NFL history. "And so, for him, the last couple of weeks maybe not getting it as much as he would maybe want − I get it, I'd be frustrated if I were him." Said Hall of Fame receiver and Vikings legend Randy Moss on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown" on Sunday morning, in a nod to Jefferson: "Whoever the quarterback is, I need you to heat my franchise player up." That was once the role of J.J. McCarthy, whom former Minnesota GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah moved up to draft 10th overall in 2024. But O'Connell quickly − prematurely? − declared Murray the winner of the team's QB competition on Aug. 11, during the very early stages of training camp. Rookie GM Nolan Teasley wasted little time offloading McCarthy, who was traded to the Giants for a mere fifth-round pick on September 28 but has now won both starts with his new team. And McCarthy sounded like a man thankful to be liberated, whether or not he should have been, from Minnesota after taking over as New York's starter going into Week 7, when he ultimately engineered an upset of the Texans in Houston. "Everything about this place it feels very fitting for me," McCarthy said of the Giants' culture, players and coaches. "(B)eing in this system where they use the quarterback's legs and a multitude of things, but the personalities, the culture of just grinding every single day to get better and everyone helping each other to progress towards one goal. It's been fantastic. A lot of successful buildings have similar qualities, and this building definitely has that. … I'm just so blessed to be a part of it." Will Vikings target a quarterback at trade deadline? Yet what if neither Murray nor Wentz is the answer for an outfit that otherwise seems to have championship-caliber talent? item.title: ‘I’m very grateful for the city of Indianapolis’: Jonathan Taylor delivers apparent goodbye to Colts
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) waves to fans as he leaves the field Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after losing a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Indianapolis Colts’ season continued to go in the wrong direction on Sunday with a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys as the team lost its fifth consecutive game. With the trade deadline just days away, Jonathan Taylor sounded like a player who knows his time in Indianapolis could be coming to an end. Speaking after the game, the star running back didn’t commit to the Colts or shoot down the trade rumors. Instead, Taylor thanked the city and its fans, saying that if Sunday was his final game with the team, he’s “very grateful” for his time there. Colts’ Fire Sale The Colts have fallen apart this season, dropping to 2-7 after Sunday’s loss. The team fired general manager Chris Ballard in October and has already traded away veteran leaders Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner for draft picks. Taylor, a three-time Pro Bowler who won the NFL rushing title in 2021, has reportedly drawn interest from multiple teams ahead of Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline. But there have been plenty of twists in the trade talks. Before Sunday’s game, Fox’s Jay Glazer reported that the New York Giants pulled their trade offer for Taylor, according to OutKick. The Giants had reportedly offered a package built around second- and fifth-round picks, but they backed off after the Colts held out for a first-rounder. Other contenders, including the Denver Broncos and Cincinnati Bengals, are reportedly still lurking. Taylor is under contract through 2028, which gives Indianapolis plenty of leverage to hold firm on its asking price. ‘Very grateful’ After the loss to Dallas, Taylor was asked about the possibility of being traded, and he didn’t stick to the usual script. “I think you play every game like it’s your last, but at the end of the day this has been a spot where I grew up,” Taylor said after the game . “I think I mentioned this to you guys, like you go to college, you’re a young man, but you really grew up, you started a family and you really embraced this city, the people, and you’re just like…” “This place helped shape me into the man I am today. If it is [my last game], I’m very grateful for the city of Indianapolis,” he continued. Taylor also made sure to thank Colts fans for their support over the years. “I just hope that they appreciate and know that I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display not only my hard work but the team’s hard work each and every single week, each and every single year. Just know it was a pleasure,” Taylor said. Needless to say, it certainly sounded like a goodbye. The post ‘I’m very grateful for the city of Indianapolis’: Jonathan Taylor delivers apparent goodbye to Colts appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Ashley Young makes concerning Senne Lammens claim after Aston Villa disasterclass
item.description: Ashley Young makes concerning Senne Lammens claim after Aston Villa disasterclass Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has seemingly questioned the mentality of goalkeeper Senne Lammens following his poor performance in the draw with Aston Villa. Senne Lammens Horror show Lammens endured a game to forget as United and Villa played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford on Sunday. He was culpable for both of Villa’s quickfire goals. The first squirmed between his legs from Alysson’s shot, and he then parried another Alysson effort into the path of the in-form Nicolas Jackson, who tapped in from close range to hand the visitors a commanding two-goal cushion. Beyond his two mistakes, Lammens repeatedly hesitated to come off his line to clear the danger, placing United at risk. The Belgium international also did not cover himself in glory for Leon Goretzka’s finish. Fortunately for United, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu came off the bench to score in stoppage time, making it 4-4 and ensuring the points were shared. Nevertheless, the Red Devils remain 18th in the Premier League and are guaranteed to occupy a place in the relegation zone for at least two weeks as the international break proceeds. Lammens’ disastrous performance was merely the latest and most damning in a growing list of displays that have left a great deal to be desired this season. Speaking on Sky Sports , Young claimed that Lammens has simply not been the same since his costly error at the World Cup with Belgium. Young’s claim The former United captain said [via Football 365 ], “For me, on the goal, Diogo Dalot, you have got to defend your goal. Slide in. Slide in. He is going in with his opposite foot.” “And then the goalkeeper doesn’t do himself any glory here.” He added, “You know, I think since the World Cup, he made that mistake, and he hasn’t looked the same as last season.” Roy Keane also stated, “Nightmare start for Utd. Obviously, never got going. Villa looked sharp. Again, the set piece, nice layoff, shot on target. The keeper has got to do better.” “And like all top strikers, you look at the reaction. He is on the move again, poor from Utd. The goalkeeper – standard save.” United are next in action on November 22 when they go away to Liverpool. Featured image by Michael Regan via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Nuggets list six key players including Nikola Jokic on injury list after getting stuck in Mexico City
item.description: Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post The Denver Nuggets are heading into a marquee Western Conference clash with major weaknesses after logistical travel issues on their way back from the 2026 NBA Mexico City Games. The Nuggets picked up a 114-102 win over the Indiana Pacers in Mexico City, one of three international regular season games played by the NBA this season. Unfortunately, the situation the Nuggets have found themselves in since the end of that game highlight how the slightest disruption during these international games can cause major issues to the routines of high-level NBA players. Nuggets get stuck in Mexico City and face major disruption before next game The Nuggets had to spend an extra 24 hours in Mexico City after their win over the Pacers on November 8 due to a number of travel issues and arrive for their road game in Houston with less than 24 hours before the game, listing most core players as questionable because of the situation . “The Nuggets have had major plane delays getting out of Mexico City, per sources, but hopeful to get out tonight. They are listing Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray, Aaron Gordon, Cam Johnson, Christian Braun and DeMar DeRozan questionable tomorrow in Houston for various minor ailments.” Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon, and Nikola Jokic are the starting five of the Nuggets while DeMar DeRozan has been their sixth man off the bench all season. Jokic is averaging 22.9 points, 10.1 rebounds and 9.1 assists this season, and his absence would be a huge blow to the 5-3 Nuggets in a big-time clash against the 7-3 Rockets. Instead of risking their core players on the court against a physical Rockets side, the Nuggets might play the long game and give their stars the rest they need instead of risking injury due to fatigue and poor recovery from two interrupted days due to travel issues. The Nuggets flight could not leave Mexico City due to an issue with the plane’s door , with the team boarding the plane at 9:00 p.m.and sat in their seats till 3:25 a.m. before being told that they could not fly that night due to the aforementioned door issue. The Nuggets landed in Houston around 6:30 p.m. local time, which is roughly 24 hours before tip-off against the Rockets, giving the players just one evening of rest before playing with no practice since before their Mexico City game. item.title: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
item.description: Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. “It’s AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati,” Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh’s formidable pass rush. “It’s good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready.” Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers’ four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. item.title: Oscar Piastri splits with Mark Webber after disappointing F1 season
item.description: Oscar Piastri has split from manager and former Formula 1 driver Mark Webber as he seeks a new direction for 2027 and beyond. Piastri, 25, has been mentored by nine-time race winner and Australian compatriot Webber since his emergence as a top prospect in junior formula and, most famously, Webber negotiated Piastri’s move to McLaren for the 2023 season, despite a tense stand-off with Alpine in the summer of 2022. Piastri was the F1 championship leader throughout most of the 2025 campaign before falling away in the final rounds, eventually finishing third, 13 points off champion and McLaren teammate Lando Norris . However, Webber has taken more of a back seat with Piastri this season, moving to a “behind the scenes” role as opposed to being ever-present at the racetrack. And Piastri has endured a tough campaign, failing to win a race and he currently sits a distant seventh in the standings, 94 points behind Norris. A statement on Monday from Webber confirmed that his partnership with Piastri has now ended. "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close," said Webber, in conjunction with his partner Ann Webber. "This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. Piastri trails Lando Norris by 94 points this season (Getty) "We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career." Piastri added: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. "Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward." Piastri’s new management structure going into the 2027 season is yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Slegers hails ‘world class’ Arsenal duo after beating Liverpool
item.description: Slegers hails ‘world class’ Arsenal duo after beating Liverpool Arsenal Women boss Renée Slegers praised Emily Fox’s attacking contribution after the full-back played a key role in both goals during the 2-1 win over Liverpool. Both of Arsenal’s goals came from deliveries from the right, with Fox and Lisa Baum providing crosses for Alessia Russo to convert. “We have world-class full-backs and we ask them to do different things for us,” Slegers said after the victory. “Sometimes it’s wide to get crosses in, sometimes it’s going inside to combine. “I thought Emily Fox was outstanding today.” Slegers was also delighted with Russo’s movement and finishing after the striker scored twice to secure the victory. “The two goals that Alessia scored, they’re so good,” she added. “She picks up good positions in the box, the finishes are so clean. “Really happy with the two goals.”

item.title: 2027: Support group targets 3.7m votes for Tinubu, Shettima
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO – A grassroots mobilisation organisation, Global Survival for Grassroots Development and Empowerment Initiative (GSGDI), has announced plans to mobilise 3.7 million votes for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in the 2027 general elections. The target was announced following the organisation’s National Executive Council conference meeting in Abuja, where its leadership mapped out strategies to mobilise 100,000 votes in each of Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The National President of GSGDI, Ahmeed Olalekan Eshinlokun, said achieving the target would require discipline, sacrifice and collective responsibility among the organisation’s executives, members and grassroots coordinators. He urged members across the country to obtain valid Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and remain actively prepared to participate in the electoral process. Eshinlokun said the organisation’s nationwide mobilisation campaign would focus on political education, community engagement and responsible democratic participation. He added that GSGDI planned to deploy its nationwide network to ensure that five representatives were assigned to every polling unit as part of its grassroots mobilisation strategy. The post 2027: Support group targets 3.7m votes for Tinubu, Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Beckham tries to recruit Dybala to Inter Miami
item.description: Beckham tries to recruit Dybala to Inter Miami Paulo Dybala’s future may lie far from Roma and Serie A. The Argentine striker, currently sidelined with a muscle injury, has reportedly been targeted by two Major League Soccer clubs. Among the most likely destinations is David Beckham’s Inter Miami, a club that also hosts Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul. This prospect could open up new horizons for the Giallorossi’s number 21, whose contract remains a key issue in the coming months. According to Radio Manà Manà , Beckham has already initiated initial contact with Dybala’s entourage to gauge the player’s willingness to move to the United States at the end of the season. The prospect of joining Messi in Florida would not be unwelcome to the Argentine, who may be considering a new professional experience after his years in the Italian league. New York City is also said to be pursuing him.

item.title: Patriots' Munich Trip Offers Chance To Rewrite International History
item.description: Patriots' Munich Trip Offers Chance To Rewrite International History originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have traveled across the Atlantic before, but their upcoming visit to Munich will bring a new experience for the franchise. New England will face the Detroit Lions on Sunday, November 15, at FC Bayern Munich Arena. It will be the Patriots' first regular-season appearance in Munich and their fifth regular-season game outside the United States. The Patriots enter the contest with a 3-1 international record, built largely during the franchise's championship era. Their only loss came during a difficult 2023 season, creating an opportunity for Drake Maye and Mike Vrabel to restore New England's winning tradition overseas. Brady Built A Perfect International Record New England's first international appearance came in 2009, when Tom Brady led the Patriots to a 35-7 victory over Tampa Bay at London's Wembley Stadium. We’re heading back to Germany 🇩🇪 Patriots vs. Lions in Munich on November 15! https://t.co/W7mpWX0Kg0 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) May 13, 2026 The Patriots returned to London in 2012 and defeated the St. Louis Rams 45-7. Five years later, they traveled to Mexico City and beat the Oakland Raiders 33-8. Those three victories produced a combined scoring margin of 113-22, a remarkable demonstration of the team's dominance during that period. Brady was the quarterback for all three wins, making the Patriots one of the most successful international teams of that era.Frankfurt Delivered A Different Experience The Patriots' most recent international appearance came against Indianapolis in Frankfurt on November 12, 2023. New England lost 10-6 in a defensive struggle that featured limited offensive production and another frustrating result during a difficult season. Mac Jones started at quarterback, and the Patriots entered their bye week with a 2-8 record. That defeat ended New England's perfect international record and provided a sharp contrast to the team's previous overseas performances. MORE : Corey Kiner’s First Patriots Touchdown Offers a Small Bright Spot in Loss Maye Gets His Opportunity The Munich game arrives during a very different period for the organization. Maye has become the central figure in New England's offense, while Vrabel is attempting to build a competitive team capable of returning to postseason contention. Detroit will provide a difficult opponent, particularly after entering November with one of the NFL's most productive offenses. The Patriots' international history is filled with memorable victories, but Munich offers an opportunity to establish a new identity. For Maye and the current roster, the challenge is not simply to celebrate what Brady accomplished abroad. It is to create another chapter worth remembering. item.title: Yobe enjoys relative peace across 17 LGAs – Buni
item.description: …Says farmers now have access to farmlands By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has said the state now enjoys relative peace across its 17 local government areas following years of insurgency, with farmers and business operators able to pursue their activities without major security disruptions. Buni spoke on Sunday night in Abuja at the Yobe Development and Partnership Roundtable, where he engaged distinguished indigenes of the state residing outside the state. He said the improved security situation had enabled farmers to return to their farmlands, while business owners could move freely across communities to conduct legitimate commercial activities. “Yobe State today enjoys relative peace across the 17 local government areas. Our farmers in the last few years have had access to their farmlands, while businessmen and women continue to traverse the length and breadth of the state conducting legitimate businesses peacefully,” the governor said. Recalling the difficult period of insurgency, Buni said the state had suffered widespread killings, displacement, destruction of communities and loss of livelihoods. “A few years back, our story was different, pathetic and despicable. Yobe, our dear state, the Pride of the Sahel, was plagued by a reckless, brutal and senseless insurgency security challenge. Many people were killed, others maimed, several communities displaced, and the surviving victims lost their means of livelihood,” he said. He, however, commended the resilience of the people, saying their determination to overcome the challenges had contributed to the state’s recovery. Buni acknowledged that rebuilding the state was difficult, considering the limited resources available to the government and the extensive destruction caused by insecurity. He said his administration supported economic recovery by distributing farm machinery and other agricultural inputs to farmers free of charge to improve productivity, strengthen food security and promote economic growth. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: …Says farmers now have access to farmlands By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has said the state now enjoys relative peace across its 17 local government areas following years of insurgency, with farmers and business operators able to pursue their activities without major security disruptions. Buni spoke on Sunday night in Abuja at the Yobe Development and Partnership Roundtable, where he engaged distinguished indigenes of the state residing outside the state. He said the improved security situation had enabled farmers to return to their farmlands, while business owners could move freely across communities to conduct legitimate commercial activities. “Yobe State today enjoys relative peace across the 17 local government areas. Our farmers in the last few years have had access to their farmlands, while businessmen and women continue to traverse the length and breadth of the state conducting legitimate businesses peacefully,” the governor said. Recalling the difficult period of insurgency, Buni said the state had suffered widespread killings, displacement, destruction of communities and loss of livelihoods. “A few years back, our story was different, pathetic and despicable. Yobe, our dear state, the Pride of the Sahel, was plagued by a reckless, brutal and senseless insurgency security challenge. Many people were killed, others maimed, several communities displaced, and the surviving victims lost their means of livelihood,” he said. He, however, commended the resilience of the people, saying their determination to overcome the challenges had contributed to the state’s recovery. Buni acknowledged that rebuilding the state was difficult, considering the limited resources available to the government and the extensive destruction caused by insecurity. He said his administration supported economic recovery by distributing farm machinery and other agricultural inputs to farmers free of charge to improve productivity, strengthen food security and promote economic growth. According to him, the government also maintained minimal tax charges for businesses and other commercial activities to enable operators to recover from the effects of the insurgency. He said the administration deliberately refrained from reviewing existing tax rates, which he described as outdated and unrealistic. On education, Buni said his administration declared a state of emergency in the sector, particularly at the primary and basic levels, upon assuming office. He listed the achievements under the programme to include the reconstruction of 301 schools, construction of 929 new classrooms and rehabilitation of 748 others. The governor added that the government established 15 mega and model schools, as well as 10 new Government Girls Senior Secondary Schools, to promote girl-child education. He said more than 9,000 qualified teachers had been recruited, while over 12,000 others received training under the emergency programme. Buni further disclosed that over 50,000 students had benefited from government scholarships, while more than 400 students were sponsored to universities in India to study medicine and engineering. He said about 200 of the beneficiaries had been employed by the state government and were already serving in medical facilities across Yobe. On healthcare, the governor said the West African College of Physicians had certified the Yobe State University Teaching Hospital for postgraduate residency training. He added that the West African College of Surgeons had also certified the Damaturu Specialist Hospital for postgraduate training of resident doctors in obstetrics and gynaecology. Buni said his administration had sustained free dialysis services for kidney patients, alongside free medical care for expectant mothers, children under five and victims of road accidents. In agriculture, he said tractors, ox-drawn ploughs, hand tillers, fertilisers and improved seeds had been distributed free of charge to farmers across the state’s 178 political wards. “We are now ready for the third phase,” he said. The governor also explained how his administration intervened to protect sesame farmers from exploitation by grain merchants from Dawanau in Kano State. He said the merchants previously visited rural communities at the end of every farming season to buy sesame crops before harvest at significantly low prices. To address the situation, Buni said the government constructed roads linking rural communities to markets, making it easier for farmers to transport their produce and secure better market access. Meanwhile, the governor announced the establishment of the Yobe Global Engagement and Partnerships Desk in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government. He said the desk would coordinate engagement with Yobe indigenes living in other parts of Nigeria and abroad, as well as institutions interested in supporting the state’s development. Buni directed the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Mohammed Goje, to develop an operational framework for the initiative, including arrangements for coordination, information management and reporting. Earlier, Goje said the roundtable was designed to provide an opportunity for the government to listen to indigenes of the state and connect their expertise with Yobe’s development priorities. “For clarity, this is an exploratory engagement. It does not seek or imply commitment,” he said. The post Yobe enjoys relative peace across 17 LGAs – Buni appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘He doesn’t want the position’: Dana White reportedly wasn’t interested President Trump’s press secretary job
item.description: Donald Trump and Dana White UFC President Donald Trump’s offer to make UFC CEO Dana White his press secretary turned out to be a joke, at least according to Trump. But it sounds like White had no interest in accepting the role anyway. According to a report this week that cited a source close to the UFC boss, White was honored by the offer but had no interest in actually taking the job – though rejecting it might have been awkward. Trump’s ‘Joke’ Offer On Saturday, Trump announced on Truth Social that he had offered White the job of White House press secretary, calling him “a violent Fighter and Warrior” and asking him to bring several UFC fighters along as assistants. “Dana, please take the job!” Trump wrote. White responded by posting an image of himself at the White House podium with the caption “On to the next chapter,” and he later said he was flying to Washington, D.C., to meet with Trump on Monday. But on Sunday, Trump told reporters that he was “only kidding” about the offer, though he added that some people thought it was “actually a pretty good idea” and that White was still coming to see him. White’s ties to Trump go back decades, and he has spoken at the last three Republican National Conventions. But after Trump’s 2024 election win, White insisted he was done with politics. “I’m never f***ing doing this again,” White told The New Yorker . “I want nothing to do with this s***. It’s gross. It’s disgusting.” ‘Absolutely crazy’ Before Trump’s walk-back, a source close to White told the Daily Mail that the UFC boss was flattered by the offer, but that it wasn’t something he wanted. “Dana is incredibly honored that the president would even consider him for a position of this magnitude,” the source said. “But the reality is that taking the job would be absolutely crazy when you consider everything he already has on his plate.” White currently runs the UFC, Power Slap, and Zuffa Boxing, and the source said that giving that up for the White House briefing room isn’t something he’s eager to do. “He doesn’t want the position, he has no desire to uproot his life and relocate, and genuinely questions whether he would have the time to give it the attention it deserves,” the source added. However, the source also claimed that White was in “a very unusual position where the opportunity might simply be too big to turn down,” and that he believed the role could help take the UFC “to an entirely new level.” “As much as he doesn’t want to do it, he may ultimately feel he has little choice but to step up, even if it’s only on a temporary basis,” the source said. “In other words, he may not want the job, but he also recognizes that saying no to Donald Trump, and an opportunity like this, isn’t quite as easy as he’d like it to be,” someone close to White told the Daily Mail. Needless to say, Trump’s “joke” appears to have taken White’s dilemma off the table. The post ‘He doesn’t want the position’: Dana White reportedly wasn’t interested President Trump’s p

item.title: “You Guys Were Chasing Him Like He Was Nick Saban”: Analyst Questions LSU’s Decision to Pursue Lane Kiffin After Disappointing Season
item.description: Dec 1, 2025; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; LSU new head coach Lane Kiffin speaks at South Stadium Club at Tiger Stadium. © Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Lane Kiffin arrived at LSU with high expectations after leaving Ole Miss, but his first season so far has not gone according to plan. Following a disappointing 31-13 loss to Alabama, questions are growing about whether the Tigers made the right decision in pursuing the head coach. ESPN analyst Scott Van Pelt has questioned the hype and investment the team made on Kiffin. During an appearance on ‘SVPod,’ Van Pelt pointed to LSU’s three losses and suggested the program’s pursuit of Kiffin was driven by expectations that have yet to translate into results on the field. “You guys were chasing him like he was Nick Saban. They’ve already got three losses, man,” Van Pelt said. The analyst also questioned what LSU could point to as a major achievement so far in Kiffin’s tenure as the Tigers struggled against some of their toughest opponents. Van Pelt acknowledged that LSU still has significant opportunities ahead, with upcoming matchups against Texas and Tennessee. However, he argued that the Tigers have not shown enough to justify the expectations surrounding Kiffin’s arrival. “To date, what’s your win? What are you hanging your hat on? Who are you pointing at and going, ‘Huh? See what we did against Clemson, A&M, McNeese?’ What do you got? Nothing. Nothing,” Van Pelt said. He said that LSU had faced three quality opponents and lost to all of them. The program made a significant investment in Kiffin with the expectation that he would immediately elevate the Tigers into national championship contention. Stanford Steve also weighed in during the discussion, agreeing that LSU and Texas had both struggled to meet the expectations placed on them before the season. He noted that the hype surrounding Kiffin and the quarterback he wanted had not translated into the results many anticipated. The criticism comes after LSU fell to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in SEC play. The Tigers have now suffered their third loss of the 2026 season, leaving their College Football Playoff hopes in a tough position. item.title: ‘On his side’ – Jaylen Brown’s blunt answer about potential conversation with Jayson Tatum
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Even after the dust around his trade has settled, Jaylen Brown isn’t willing to engage with his former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum. Tatum and Brown played together for nine years, reaching five Eastern Conference Finals, two NBA Finals, and winning an NBA Championship in 2024. The All-NBA pair was considered one of the best in the league, but Brown’s departure from the Celtics has exposed just how frail their relationship was over their nine-year stint together. Jaylen Brown claims he won’t speak to Jayson Tatum before 76ers vs. Celtics game Speaking to reporters after the Philadelphia 76ers beat the Chicago Bulls, Jaylen Brown was asked about facing the Boston Celtics for the first time, and how he plans to reunite with Jayson Tatum. Brown suggested he still hasn’t spoken with Tatum since his departure, and has no reason or interest in speaking with his former All-Star teammate. Brown curtly said: “Nope (when asked if he and Jayson Tatum had talked since NBA Media Day). There’s nothing to talk about. He’s on his side, and I’m on my side playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win, so there’s nothing to talk about. Check the ball up. “I love Boston. Boston is a great city. A lot of great people I’ve developed relationships with. I’m just focused on what is in front of me right now. That’s the most important thing…” Brown has made his issues with Tatum and the Celtics no secret, even if he hasn’t openly discussed what exactly went wrong between the two. At one point, Brown and Tatum appeared to be good friends, with their on-court chemistry reflecting that very well. But the pair clearly have some unresolved issues and will try to get the better of each other when the 76ers face the Celtics this week. item.title: Kentucky vs. Florida game glance, opening odds, and early prediction
item.description: Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they’ll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their mind, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone’s guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Florida Gators Location: Kroger Field- Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 14th Time: 6:15 PM ET TV: ESPN Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel Sportsbook has Kentucky favored by 3.5 points with an over/under of 51.5. ESPN win probability: ESPN FPI gives Kentucky a 54% chance of victory Our prediction I’m not going to lie, this game has got weirdness written all over it. Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6’6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side

Ultimately, I think Kentucky does clean it up, and despite some pressure off the edge, the Cats knock off the Gators. Final score: Kentucky 33, Florida 21 Which team do you think bounces back best from a tough loss?

item.title: Bronny James Claps Back At Pistons Fan: “How Much Money You Make A Year?”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Bronny James didn’t feature in the Los Angeles Lakers ‘ 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday, but he still ended up making headlines. Bronny had some choice words for a Pistons fan during the game, as he appeared to get into a back-and-forth with one of them. “Can you run a mile?” Bronny said. “How much money you make a year?” BRONNY JAMES SNAPPED ON A FAN COURT SIDE TONIGHT 😭 “How much money you make a year?” LMFAOOOOOOOO #LakeShow — FADE (@FadeAwayMedia) November 9, 2026 It’s unclear what the Pistons fan said to spark such a reaction from Bronny, who isn’t known to lose his cool. The 22-year-old’s last notable interaction with a heckler involved him hilariously telling the individual their chain was fake . He has developed some thick skin over the years, but Lakers staffers had to restrain him here. Bronny, who is making $2.3 million in 2026-27, seemed to mock the fan’s weight with the “running a mile” comment and then delivered the typical athlete taunt about money. According to the video, the fan was later ejected from the game. This was the second time in three games that a fan was ejected from a Lakers game. During Wednesday’s 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center, a fan was tossed for aggressively throwing the ball at official Chelisa Painter . Lakers superstar Luka Doncic confronted the fan for the act, and security seemingly ushered him out not long after. Now, Doncic didn’t play against the Pistons here due to lower back tightness, and you wondered if Bronny might get some game time as a result, but he didn’t. He watched from the bench as the Lakers won 121-116 to improve to 9-2. Austin Reaves led the way in Doncic’s absence with 43 points (14-27 FG), five rebounds, and four assists against the Pistons. Reaves had a viral confrontation with a Pistons fan , too, but this individual wasn’t ejected. Now, this was the Lakers’ 11th game of the season, and Bronny has only played in five of them. That’s not a good sign. Bronny is averaging just 0.8 points and 0.2 blocks per game in 2026-27, and it’s quite clear that Lakers head coach JJ Redick does not trust him at the moment. He made some progress in his sophomore campaign, but is out of the rotation now. The Lakers even assigned Bronny and rookie Cameron Carr to their G League affiliate , the Coachella Valley Lakers, on Friday, ahead of their season opener against the Salt Lake City Stars. They helped the team get off to a winning start, taking down the Stars 104-98. Bronny put up 22 points (8-18 FG), five rebounds, seven assists, and one steal in the win. It was a fine performance, and his critics would argue the G League is where he belongs, not the NBA. Bronny has faced nepotism allegations throughout his short NBA career. The Lakers selected him with the No. 55 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, and many believe they picked him only to please his father, LeBron James . LeBron then left for the Phila

item.title: Who slept best last night: Toto Wolff
item.description: Motorsport photo Toto Wolff didn't need to brag when, on Sunday evening in Sao Paulo, he was asked about his records, which now put him alongside two of F1's greats. The question of how it feels to match Frank Williams' tally of constructors' championships and Ron Dennis' overall number of titles was enough in itself to illustrate the magnitude of Wolff's achievements. He now has nine constructors' titles, level with Williams , and 17 titles overall, matching Dennis. "When I think about it, these two are giants of the sport," he said. "I'm not even operating in the same galaxy as Frank, who after his accident, has been able to achieve great things. And in the same way, Ron is a person that [you] always look up to who has been the benchmark in the sport, who has set new standards." He added: "I will never see myself in that league." Formula 1 has changed enormously since the days when those two were winning titles and trying to beat each other. It might be an oversimplification, but nowadays it's much more about running an efficient business than running the best garage. They, too, had to secure sponsorship deals and attract the best talent, but modern F1 operations, especially a works team with its own engine department, are many times more complex. The sheer difference in employee numbers is staggering. Wolff has no chance of knowing everyone working for his team and can't rely on the kind of micromanagement that was perhaps still possible in the 1980s. It requires a different skill set, a much clearer understanding of what's called "culture", and far greater precision in building an organisation in which delegation is not just a tool, but a necessity. But what Dennis and Williams have in common is that they didn't just win titles in succession, at the peak of their teams' performance, when everything aligned. They did it repeatedly, rebuilding the organisations they led to come back and win again. Williams did it after splitting with Honda, returning to the top with Renault. Dennis did it after the Alain Prost and Ayrton Senna era, rebuilding McLaren to win three titles with Mika Hakkinen and Mercedes . Wolff is probably right in the sense that he has never had to deal with a complete reorganisation involving a change of major partners or engine manufacturer. But the 2026 season is the ultimate proof that he, too, is not someone who can only do it once. Toto Wolff, Mercedes Toto Wolff, Mercedes Mercedes didn't hit rock bottom. But after winning so easily and so consistently, the team may have become too set in its ways to change and adapt. The new regulation cycle in 2022 was a stress test it failed – and the old methods were no longer working when it came to catching up. We'll never know exactly what Wolff did or which processes needed to change. We can only judge by the results. And 2026 is confirmation that he did what was required. Wolff is probably right in the sense that he has never had to deal with a complete reorganisation involving a change of major partners or engine manufacturer. But the 2026 season is the ultimate proof that he, too, is not someone who can only do it once. Toto Wolff, Mercedes Toto Wolff, Mercedes Mercedes didn't hit rock bottom. But after winning so easily and so consistently, the team may have become too set in its ways to change and adapt. The new regulation cycle in 2022 was a stress test it failed – and the old methods were no longer working when it came to catching up. We'll never know exactly what Wolff did or which processes needed to change. We can only judge by the results. And 2026 is confirmation that he did what was required. "Looking back, I think those last four years were very difficult," he said on Sunday. "Between getting it wrong and then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising, no, we didn't understand... And that was a big back and forth. "But we will be looking back in 10 or 20 years, and when you look at the statistics, it wasn't that we were complete losers over those four years, because we finished second, third, third, fourth - I think that was maybe what the results were. We won races, won many races. So it wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good. "And the resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times is a factor, I think. So it feels really good sealing those two titles. "Not many sports teams have done that after a consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell, and then coming back. So I'm really proud that we are part of this very small group of teams that have done that in all sports." Even if he isn't in quite the same league yet, he's certainly among the very best team bosses in F1 history. George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Culture is a word often used and abused by managers, many of whom don't really understand what it entails. But it's not just a matter of principles and rules. It's about choosing a common goal, putting the right processes in place, finding the best people and helping them fulfil their ambitions – and being committed to all of it. There are plenty of people who say they want to build "a culture". Far fewer actually understand what they mean by that. "We are not a hire-and-fire organisation," Wolff says. "We provide a culture and an environment where you can thrive, where you are allowed to make mistakes, where you can speak up. And over the long term, I believe, if you want to be successful, not over a period of a few years but over many decades, this is what you need to be able to kind of ingrain in the team. "And we are trying that. It's not something you put on a PowerPoint. You have to lift your standards day in and day out. And these are the standards we are setting to ourselves. Sometimes we fail, but we look at the long-term vision." Again, seeing only the tip of the iceberg isn't enough to judge exactly how much of this is Wolff's doing. But that culture of helping people thrive – which also means supporting those who are struggling – is on display. The way Wolff handles George Russell , probably the only member of the Mercedes F1 team who wasn't entirely happy on Sunday, is a textbook example of managing talent, too. It's been a tough year for Russell, no doubt about that. But Wolff keeps an arm around his shoulder and never gives the outside world any reason to doubt that he still believes in him – even though some suggest he only cares about Antonelli. George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes "It's George's championship today," Toto said. "It's the constructors' championship, and he's part of the team, and I'm really happy that he can cherish this moment, because we owe it to him." And he added: "I have no doubt about that for next year, and all the very best sports people have gone through difficult periods, and that's going to be part of his continued development." And listen to George himself. His Sao Paulo weekend was perhaps a perfect illustration of his 2026 season. Flashes of speed, but circumstances beyond his control preventing him from getting the result – as happened on Saturday – and some mistakes of his own, as at the pit exit on Sunday. But the way he speaks about Wolff leaves little doubt that he feels that trust, too. On Saturday, when 2026 dealt him another blow in the form of a missed pole position, he still spoke more about the bigger picture than the incident itself: "I think something I admire a lot from Toto's leadership is the people we have today are the same people who were there during the glory years, and they're the same people who went through the difficulties during 2022 to 2025. "Nobody was hired and fired. The trust and belief stayed with the core group of people, and, you know, now we've come through. And, you know, obviously, Kimi won the championship. We are going to win the championship, whether it's this weekend or next. And, you know, credit to everybody in the team, but yeah, huge credit to Toto for that loyalty and belief in the people, even when times were tough." That loyalty and belief is exactly what Wolff is showing Russell right now. And Russell's career could still follow one of two very different paths: that of Nico Rosberg or that of Daniel Ricciardo .
