item.title: 🚨 Lamine Yamal and Oyarzabal, out of Spain's clash with Czechia
item.description: 🚨 Lamine Yamal and Oyarzabal, out of Spain's clash with Czechia Spain’s national team training camp began on Monday with two notable absences from Luis de la Fuente’s plans. Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal have delayed joining up with ‘La Roja’ and will not be part of the squad travelling to Prague to face the Czech Republic this Thursday (20:45), on matchday five of the UEFA Nations League group stage. Lamine Yamal finished FC Barcelona’s win over Atlético de Madrid at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano with knee discomfort. As a medical precaution, the coaching and medical staff have decided that the player should remain in Barcelona for treatment. Meanwhile, Mikel Oyarzabal remains in San Sebastián with flu symptoms that have prevented him from travelling to the capital to join team training at the Ciudad del Fútbol in Las Rozas. Both players are expected to be available against England next Sunday, November 15, at 20:45. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: “Just Lost His MVP Bid,” “Getting Carried by Defense”: NFL Fans React As Caleb Williams Throws 4 INTs in Bears’ Win vs. Buccaneers
item.description: Caleb Williams Bears © Imagn Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams struggled with multiple interceptions in Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite the quarterback’s disastrous night, the Bears pulled off a dramatic 27-24 victory. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions. The Bears signal-caller completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns. Williams’ interceptions allowed Tampa Bay to come back after trailing 17-6 at halftime. NFL fans reacted to Williams’ underwhelming performance in the Bears’ win. “Caleb Williams just lost his MVP bid,” one fan wrote. “Caleb Williams getting CARRIED by his defense,” another fan added. “It’s no way Caleb Williams can throw 4 picks, have his team still win, and be in MVP conversation. That’s being carried, which is the opposite of what MVP is,” one fan noted. “Once again showing Caleb Williams gets carried by his team..💀 unethical hooper,” one fan remarked. “Caleb Williams MVP stock dropping tonight,” one fan added. “Caleb Williams MVP talk should die after this. This team needs to be humble,” one fan commented. Many fan conversations focused on Williams hurting his MVP chances with his performance on Sunday. However, those hopes may be doomed for now after he threw four picks. According to USA Today , it was the first time in his career, including his time in college football, that he threw this many interceptions. Last season, he threw three interceptions in the game that ended last year’s NFC divisional-round loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He also had three interceptions in a loss to Notre Dame during his final season at USC. Caleb Williams Redeems Himself With Clutch Pass In Bucs Win Caleb Williams’ Chicago entered halftime with a 17-6 lead, but Tampa Bay’s second-half surge made things interesting. After Williams threw his fourth interception, Jaylon Johnson intercepted Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield and returned it 67 yards for a touchdown. Tampa Bay’s Bucky Irving responded with his second rushing touchdown with 2:51 remaining to tie the game at 24-24, also thanks to Mayfield’s two-point conversion. With the game potentially heading into overtime, Williams put the Bears in field goal range in Tampa Bay territory. He did so when he connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain. Chicago’s kicker Cairo Santos did the rest, hitting the game-winning 38-yard field goal to secure the Bears’ 27-24 win. As a result, Chicago improved to 7-2, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-6. item.title: Most overrated/underrated teams in Week 10 coaches poll
item.description: After Week 10, we still don't quite know where the college football season will take us. What we do know though is that there may be more teams than ever in the reckoning for a top 12 CFP spot. Yet another No. 1 team has gone down, with Miami losing to Notre Dame on the road. Behind them, even more chaos could ensue, with both Alabama and Texas staying alive and Ohio State essentially getting eliminated. Oh yeah, and Utah and UCLA remain the only undefeated teams in the country. Here are the most overrated and underrated teams in yet another crazy coaches poll. Overrated: No. 6 Miami Well, you kind of had to expect the fact that once Miami played a solid team, they may falter. That was the case yesterday as even a furious comeback couldn't lift the Hurricanes past a determined Notre Dame squad. Even though Darian Mensah threw three second half touchdown passes, sans Malachi Toney, he did not play a consistent game and looked rattled early in the matchup. For now, Miami shouldn't feel too bad about their CFP chances, but they must ensure that they win the ACC because there may not be margin for error for a two loss ACC runner up. Underrated: No. 4 UCLA Is UCLA really this good? They just might be. They many not have the best strength of schedule or of record, but they get the job done week in week out. Ever since Nico Iamaleava's injury, Ty Dieffenbach has played safe, efficient football. Yesterday though, it was his time to shine. On only 8 total completions, he had a total of 303 yards and three touchdowns. In fact, two of UCLA's drives were 75 yard dimes for Dieffenbach. Voters continue to underestimate the Bruins at their own peril. It's now not funny that they're continuing to be disregarded. Overrated: No. 20 Ohio State For the first time in 12 years, Ohio State have reached an unheard of nadir. This is the lowest they have been ranked this late in a season since then, and while there have been a lot of determining factors, this team looks nothing like a CFP contender, let alone a top 25 team. It feels weird considering that Luke Fahey really is not at fault, and yet is helpless to find a way to uplift this squad. Add in a frustrated Jeremiah Smith and a defense that looks wholly different than they did to start the season, and you get a very sticky situation in Columbus. Underrated: No. 23 South Carolina The resurgence of the Gamecocks is one that could see them be a point of contention amongst the committee by year's end. While they have three losses on their resume, they've been able to rebound in spirited fashion. LaNorris Sellers has also rejuvenated his season, throwing for 11 touchdowns and only three interceptions during this four game winning streak. It was his emotionally gritty touchdown run that lifted the Gamecocks over Texas A&M and kept them on the right track to end the season. On the other hand, Sellers was gimpy for most of the second half with an ankle injury, so who knows if he'll be able to gut it out the rest of the way

A win over a solid Big 12 team is a win, but there has been nothing to convince me that Texas Tech is the clear favorite in the conference. Besides, their best win is against Houston, who's definitely not the same as a Notre Dame or a BYU. Chances are the Red Raiders have to win out to be safely in the CFP. Once they get there though, expect a swift exit. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . item.title: ‘Morally bankrupt’: NFL criticized for chasing Taylor Swift fans as Josh Jacobs plays through abuse allegations
item.description: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The NFL has worked hard to grow its female fanbase in recent years, and Taylor Swift’s relationship with Travis Kelce has been a big part of that. But according to one columnist, the league is undermining all of that progress with how it has handled the situation regarding Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. This week, Jacobs was back on the field for the Green Bay Packers despite new abuse allegations from three women, which surfaced just days after he returned from a six-game absence. In a new column, Daily Mail US deputy sports editor Rich Jones argued that the situation is “more proof the league is morally bankrupt.” Josh Jacobs’ Return Jacobs was arrested in May after an altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. In September, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property, and he spent the first six games of the season on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. Shortly after Jacobs returned, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department released records from its investigation that included accounts from three other women describing similar allegations from previous years, according to NFL.com . The NFL has said that it will review the new allegations as part of its ongoing investigation. Jacobs has denied the new allegations, saying that they feel “like an attack” on him. His lawyers called the accounts “old,” “hearsay,” and “easily disproven,” and said they have a “substantial body of tangible evidence” to dispute them. In the meantime, Jacobs has continued to play. He scored a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers in his second game back and celebrated with a handcuff gesture, which he later insisted was unrelated to his case and was a reference to a gospel song. ‘Morally bankrupt’ In his column for the Daily Mail , Jones wrote that the Jacobs situation shows how quickly NFL teams overlook off-field issues when a player can help them win. “While the NFL investigates the latest allegations, and he remains innocent until proven guilty, the fact Jacobs is still stepping out onto the field paints both the league and the Packers in a bad light,” Jones wrote. “And it does little to dispel the idea that, ultimately, moral compass flies out the window if a player is deemed useful and valuable on the field.” Jones also pointed to the Kansas City Chiefs, who recently signed kicker Justin Tucker after he served a 10-game suspension over multiple allegations of sexual misconduct involving massage therapists, which Tucker has called “unequivocally false.” That move drew plenty of criticism as well. “These incidents are, sadly, nothing new. Listing those with alleged checkered pasts still suiting up on a weekly basis would be a long and near-impossible task,” Jones wrote. “But the ongoing Jacobs saga is another high-profile and sorry chapter that undermines the work the league has done to appeal to more female fans.” Jones noted that the NFL has “leaned h

Listing those with alleged checkered pasts still suiting up on a weekly basis would be a long and near-impossible task,” Jones wrote. “But the ongoing Jacobs saga is another high-profile and sorry chapter that undermines the work the league has done to appeal to more female fans.” Jones noted that the NFL has “leaned heavily into the ‘Taylor Swift effect’ since 2023,” when Swift attended her first Chiefs game to support Kelce. The league has since hit its highest female viewership since it started collecting data in 2000. “And so what message does it send to those millions of women, to be watching someone facing harrowing accusations of battery?” Jones asked. Clearly, Jones doesn’t think the NFL can have it both ways. item.title: LSU sweeps fall baseball doubleheader against Troy
item.description: Following a successful weekend in Biloxi, Jay Johnson’s Tigers returned home for a Sunday doubleheader. LSU welcomed in Troy for two 9-inning games. Although they lost a good amount of their impact players, the Trojans are coming off of an Omaha visit, making it to the College World Series for the first time in program history just 5 months ago. The Tigers took both games of the doubleheader in what was a beautiful day at the Box. It was a late inning comeback in game 1 with LSU down 9-5 in the 8th inning, but a 3-run homerun by their leader, Steven Milam, got them within striking distance for the 9th. Notre Dame transfer, Bino Watters, made his purple and gold debut this weekend and could not have gotten off to a better start. With two outs in the 9th, he walked it off with a 2-run single to clinch a 10-9 victory. LSU got a strong start by William Schmidt, with impressive relief appearances by Diego Velazquez and Lucas Nawrocki to bookend the game on the mound. Nawrocki has flashed his ability to be a 2-way player this fall and that was on display in this one, as he started at DH and went 1-2 with a triple at the plate, then pitched the final inning in which he struck out the side to eventually get credited with the win. The second game of the day was all Tigers from the very beginning. Last year’s ace, Casan Evans, made his second fall appearance and was dominant, striking out 5 in just 2.0 innings of work. Cooper Sides and Braxton Beaty followed him up by combining for 4 innings of no hit baseball, including 7 strikeouts. After a shaky outing from Kaden Smith, Ethan Plog took over to close out the game by also not allowing a hit and striking out 3. The offense got out to a hotter start in the second game than they did the first. That was in large part to Nawrocki, who led off with a solo homerun after closing out game 1 on the mound. Watters delivered 2 more hits, making it 5 total on the day. Jason Wachs, Dominic Santarelli, and Parker Loew each drove in runs later in the game, helping the Tigers complete the sweep with a 9-3 final score. I will have more in-depth breakdown of each pitcher individually, along with the offensive stars, to follow this short recap. Below will be the cumulative stats for each game. As I normally do, I’ll attach my quick recap video that I film afterwards, along with our press availability with Jay Johnson. Stay tuned for more to follow soon after this. Game 1 (LSU 10-9) Pitching William Schmidt: 2.0 IP / 1 hit / 0 runs / 4 K / 0 BB / 28 pitches (21 strikes, 75%) Logan Schmidt: 0.2 IP / 3 hits / 4 runs / 1 K / 1 BB / 1 HBP / 23 pitches (11 strikes, 48%) Landon Hood: 2.0 IP / 1 hit / 2 runs / 3 K / 1 BB / 1 HBP / 37 pitches (23 strikes, 62%) Danny Lachenmayer: 1.0 IP / 4 hits / 3 runs / 1 K / 1 HBP / 30 pitches (18 strikes, 60%) Diego Velazquez: 2.0 IP / 2 hits / 0 runs / 3 K / 1 BB / 42 pitches (23 strikes, 55%) Lucas Nawrocki: 1.0 IP / 2 hits / 0 runs / 3 K / 0 BB / 18 pitches (14 strikes, 78%) Hitting Bino Watte

item.title: The state of the atmosphere at St James’ Park, Selhurst Park and what can be done?
item.description: Newcastle Fans St. James' Park Pre Match Reading Greg McPeake’s article on The Mag (‘ Interesting what these Chelsea fans had to say in the pub the other week’ – 1 Nov) about Chelsea fans giving up their season tickets because they’ve become too expensive, made me think about recurring comments on The Mag and elsewhere about Newcastle United fans and the changing demographics inside St James’ Park on match day. One description that I’ve seen seems to sum up both the change and the general effect this may be having – that we now have a stadium full of spectators rather than fans. This was part of the case argued by Chris Hall in his article ( ‘An open letter to Newcastle United fans’ – 8 Nov) which examined in detail what he sees as the changed atmosphere generated nowadays at St James Park and the reasons for that. Reaction to that article was, unsurprisingly polarised, with people either praising it for hitting the nail on the head or slamming it as uninformed “bobbins”! Chris was either exposing the reality of the “Fortress SJP” myth, or exposing his own lack of real experience in a frantic effort to blame the Newcastle United fans for the club’s failings. Take your pick. I’m not setting out to insult or denigrate anyone by bringing up this issue. I’m well aware that, despite the continuing emphasis on growing the commercial side of match day, the stadium is still rammed with tens of thousands of passionate Geordies – but as season ticket holders of long standing they are inevitably growing longer in the tooth. The passion is, maybe, now internalised and reserved for the more extreme moments rather than roaring out in youthful exuberance throughout the match. Thus speaks the man who hasn’t ventured inside St James’ Park since the day that internalised passion was released to roundly boo off Moussa Sissoko during a dire home defeat to Bournemouth! I would also like to point out, though, that any reservations regarding the home supporters as a body do NOT apply to the away fans who often show up the home supporters in their own grounds. Anyway, my aim here wasn’t to focus so much on our supporters but to raise the issue in a wider context, using the example of another club who we played recently – Crystal Palace. item.content:encoded: Newcastle Fans St. James' Park Pre Match Reading Greg McPeake’s article on The Mag (‘ Interesting what these Chelsea fans had to say in the pub the other week’ – 1 Nov) about Chelsea fans giving up their season tickets because they’ve become too expensive, made me think about recurring comments on The Mag and elsewhere about Newcastle United fans and the changing demographics inside St James’ Park on match day. One description that I’ve seen seems to sum up both the change and the general effect this may be having – that we now have a stadium full of spectators rather than fans. This was part of the case argued by Chris Hall in his article ( ‘An open letter to Newcastle United fans’ – 8 Nov) which examined in detail what he sees as the changed atmosphere generated nowadays at St James Park and the reasons for that. Reaction to that article was, unsurprisingly polarised, with people either praising it for hitting the nail on the head or slamming it as uninformed “bobbins”! Chris was either exposing the reality of the “Fortress SJP” myth, or exposing his own lack of real experience in a frantic effort to blame the Newcastle United fans for the club’s failings. Take your pick. I’m not setting out to insult or denigrate anyone by bringing up this issue. I’m well aware that, despite the continuing emphasis on growing the commercial side of match day, the stadium is still rammed with tens of thousands of passionate Geordies – but as season ticket holders of long standing they are inevitably growing longer in the tooth. The passion is, maybe, now internalised and reserved for the more extreme moments rather than roaring out in youthful exuberance throughout the match. Thus speaks the man who hasn’t ventured inside St James’ Park since the day that internalised passion was released to roundly boo off Moussa Sissoko during a dire home defeat to Bournemouth! I would also like to point out, though, that any reservations regarding the home supporters as a body do NOT apply to the away fans who often show up the home supporters in their own grounds. Anyway, my aim here wasn’t to focus so much on our supporters but to raise the issue in a wider context, using the example of another club who we played recently – Crystal Palace. Being a self-professed expert on the state of places I don’t actually go to, I have for years regarded Selhurst Park as one of the last bastions (at Premier League level) of the “real” game. An old fashioned stadium in the heart of the local community with what seems to be an energetic and noisy working class fan base. It certainly comes over that way on the TV and I always enjoy the passion and volume of the Palace fans. Despite their recent trophy successes – or maybe I should be saying BECAUSE of those successes – Palace are currently struggling in the Premier League. Midweek European games on top of season after season selling their best players has finally caught up with them, it would seem. Things have become so bad that they even contrived to lose at home …… to us! When reading the Palace fans’ post-match comments on The Mag. I was struck by two references in particular regarding the atmosphere. One referred to our supporters completely out-singing theirs and offering up the ditty, “shall we sing a song for you?” I must say, it was noticeable on the TV that our guys were consistently louder than theirs – something I don’t normally expect at Selhurst Park. In contrast with Darren Henderson’s assertion, in what I thought was an excellent article , ( ‘Newcastle United on the road to nowhere via Putney Bridge’ ) published on The Mag on Bonfire Night, that our away support has become “stagnant”, my ears confirmed that it was very much vibrant and in full flow at Selhurst Park on this occasion at least. Some other comments set me off on understanding why this was possible. These other comments referred to the absence of the “HF”. Visitors to Selhurst Park will know that the popular end of the ground is the Holmsdale Road end and that Palace have a tradition of their most committed supporters gathering there and being orchestrated by a core group of “ultras” known as the Holmsdale Fanatics. Ultras are very much a European phenomenon – the hard core of the home support, inevitably dressed primarily in black and using a variety of aids, such as drums, megaphones, pyrotechnics and “choirmasters”, to increase noise levels and lead the support within the stadium. They are not generally associated with British teams. Indeed, new Palace manager Pierre Sage stated that a key reason he decided to take charge of the club is because it was one of the only clubs in the Premier League that had ultras. He didn’t mention salary …. The group was founded in December 2005 by a small number of supporters who had attended matches together since childhood in the 1980s. They traditionally stood in Block B of the Holmsdale Road Stand since 1999 but have had a bit of a running battle with the club, especially following stadium regulations introduced as a result of the Taylor report, which they described as restrictive. They have since been relocated within that end of the ground in, I believe, Block E. It is this group that has been responsible for the organised displays and coordinated support that has generated much of the energy and noise that I have always associated with the Selhurst Park home crowd. However, that has sadly now (for Palace fans at least) come to an end. On 28 Aug 2026, they announced that they were disbanding. The Sun quoted their spokesman as stating: “Increasingly driven out by the sky high ticket prices, needless restrictions that are designed to strip away the dignity of supporters and relentless harassment and legal action, many young people are choosing to opt out of a game which seems determined to push them away. “There needs to be a drastic shift at Palace towards younger fans and a move away from a culture in which people attend the ground expecting to be entertained, towards a culture of supporters turning up to play an active role in influencing the result.” Ticket price rises forcing traditional, working class supporters and youngsters away. Longstanding supporters having to give up season tickets as referenced by Greg’s Chelsea supporting pals. Youngsters being priced out of match day and being replaced by “tourists” prepared to pay the commercial rates for a one-off experience. These are familiar refrains – not just emanating from Monkseaton but increasingly from all other corners of Geordieland. Spectators rather than fans! The quote continues, elaborating on the issue of mounting displays and using flags and banners during the match: “From fighting for the most basic of rights just to take materials into Selhurst and stand up in Block B in the early days, to never ending problems with the club right up to the present day, we have been uncompromising in fighting for what we believe in and the rights of football supporters everywhere.” Newcastle Fan Walking Up Stairs At St James’ Park, Wor Flags suspended their activities due to Mike Ashley and his lack of support for Rafa Benitez in particular. Fortunately, they were not just welcomed back by the new owners but positively encouraged. The Holmsdale Fanatics have clearly not enjoyed that kind of relationship with the Palace hierarchy. For whatever reason, I would argue that this has been to the detriment of the club because of the consequent deterioration, now, in the match day atmosphere. Another key issue that crops up in relation to clubs throughout the country is an inevitable outcome of the aforementioned Taylor Report and that is the fact that, due to the requirement for grounds to be all seater, it is impossible for groups of like-minded supporters to simply gather together within the stadia and choose where they sit/stand (even in home areas of safe standing). “But the current set up is unsustainable. item.title: Pirates 2B Brandon Lowe among potential free agent busts
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 13: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates looks on during the seventh inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on September 13, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Isaac Wasserman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe is a free agent this offseason, and the team could look to re-sign him or let him walk to another team on the open market. Lowe, 32, enjoyed a breakout year with the Pirates, where he had 5.3 wins above replacement, a career high for the 9-year veteran. In 150 appearances for the Pirates, he had a batting average of .260, 35 home runs, and 96 runs batted in. His strong showing in a contract year makes him one of the top free-agent infielders available, but that could be a flash in the pan. It’s very possible we may have seen the best of Lowe already. Bleacher Report contributor Zachary D. Rymer listed Lowe as one of the top eight potential free agent busts in the league this offseason. “The bad stuff concerns what happened when Lowe didn’t make contact. His 28.8 K% marked his highest strikeout rate since 2019, and it might undersell how much he swung and missed. He had a 66.9 contact percentage, third-lowest among qualified hitters,“ Rymer wrote. “That would be easy to forgive if Lowe had good plate discipline, but his 33.6 chase percentage was a career high and in the 27th percentile to boot. That’s never ideal, and least of all for a 32-year-old whose “old man skills” should be getting sharper.“ Lowe is expected to get many strong offers in free agency, which could poach him from the Pirates, who would love to re-sign him but at a reasonable price tag. Other teams may offer Lowe a much larger bag, which could mean he is one-and-done in Pittsburgh. These concerns might be part of the reason why the Pirates are hesitant to give him a larger deal, but they have their number in mind for him when negotiations begin in the offseason.

item.title: Beyond the Asphalt: How Jetour’s High-Octane Lagos Convoy Brought Clean Water and Hope to Iwerekun Orile.
item.description: On Saturday, September 19, 2026, the roar of modern horsepower met the rhythm of drumming and celebration in Iwerekun Orile, Ibeju Lekki. Jetour Nigeria proved that the ultimate destination of any journey isn’t just where the road ends, it’s the lives transformed along the way. As part of the “2026 Jetour Africa Expedition: A Road Trip Beyond Limits,” a striking fleet featuring the Jetour Dashing, X50, X70 Plus, X90 Plus, T2, T2 PHEV, X70 PHEV, and the flagship G700, embarked on an ambitious test of endurance. Following a vital road safety briefing by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Deputy Corps Commander Zonal Training Officer, Lagos, Mrs Esther Uzoma, and with seamless escort from the Nigeria Police Force and LASTMA, the convoy rolled out of Falomo Square, Ikoyi, turning heads across Victoria Island before pushing past the city’s glossy borders. Drivers and enthusiasts left the comfort of tarmac behind, putting the SUVs to the ultimate test across the unforgiving, swampy, and rock-strewn trails of the Coastal Highway. Yet, the real test of the day wasn’t mechanical resilience; it was human connection. The convoy’s final stop was the Roman Catholic Mission Primary School in Iwerekun Orile, where dust and exhaustion gave way to unbridled joy. There, Jetour officially commissioned a brand new, solar-powered borehole, delivering clean, reliable running water to a community that has spent generations yearning for it. The reception was deeply moving. School children broke into vibrant cultural dances, welcoming the convoy alongside elders, farmers, and market women. Beyond water, the team distributed food supplies to households, while pupils beamed with arms full of new books and refreshments. “This is where adventure meets purpose,” said Jetour Nigeria representative Kemi Adeola. “Our mission doesn’t stop at building capable vehicles; it lives in our pledge to drive tangible progress and touch the hearts of the communities we reach.” For the community, the impact was profound. High Chief Michael Oluwa hailed the water project as an unprecedented miracle in Iwerekun Orile’s history, pledging that the community would cherish and protect it. Equally overcome with emotion was the school’s head teacher, Mrs. Ariyike Bakre. “This is a special lifetime gift,” Bakre said, moved by the sight of water flowing on the school grounds. “It’s my first time seeing a solar-powered borehole. I am grateful to God for making this possible in my time, and for allowing our elders to witness this day. We cannot thank Jetour Nigeria enough, this water changes everything for our children and our people.” The day wound down at a tranquil beach lounge, where drivers and organizers gathered to celebrate the journey over good food, music, and shared memories. It was a fitting close to an unforgettable expedition: one that conquered demanding terrain, ignited the spirit of adventure, and left behind a lasting lifeline of clean water. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Torrent underground
item.description: When Jane first heard about Memory and Imagination , a rare 1990s documentary about the Library of Congress, she was intrigued. But the Canadian writer in her 30s couldn’t find the movie anywhere — not on streaming services, not on YouTube, not on pirate sites — and her intrigue turned into obsession. Worried it might become a lost film , Jane decided to scour auction sites, search every library catalog she could think of, and even enlist some of her online acquaintances to find a copy. Her plan was to “share it with other people to help ensure it would be preserved into the future,” as she puts it. Jane knew the perfect tool for the task: a private torrent tracker. “I am ethically conflicted about piracy. I often feel guilty about it.” Private trackers are essentially the speakeasies of the online piracy world. Promoted primarily by word of mouth, they rely on secrecy, exclusivity, and strict community rules to shield everything that’s going on behind closed doors from the public’s prying eyes. What unites these communities is that they all use BitTorrent to trade media among like-minded file sharers. But their focuses range widely, from general-purpose trackers with catalogs so broad that they make Netflix look like a niche service to the many specialized communities for categories like Chinese movies, motorsports, visual effects tools, e-learning courses, and Japanese porn. There’s even a private tracker just for Frank Zappa music. Private trackers are known for massive and meticulously organized catalogs, which they owe to users like Jane, who, like every other pirate I talked to for this story, opted to be identified by a pseudonym due to the terabytes of copyrighted data they’ve been sharing. These are people willing to go the extra mile to find long-forgotten movies, rare concert recordings, or out-of-print books. “Many private tracker users are fully consumed with archive fever,” she says. At first, Jane had no luck finding a physical copy of that elusive documentary, which includes interviews with Steve Jobs and Julia Child. Nobody was selling it on eBay. Her local public library didn’t have it. Neither did any other public library in North America. And when she finally located a DVD that was available to the public, it was in the Bibliotheca Alexandrina — Egypt’s modern-day re-creation of the ancient library that’s long been synonymous with lost media. “That bowled me over,” Jane says. “This obscure movie I’m looking for is only available in the Library of Alexandria!” Eventually, Jane found Memory and Imagination for sale on a small online marketplace for historical media. Jane instantly bought a copy and uploaded it. “It looked like a digital rip of a severely degraded VHS tape,” she says. “I was still over the moon [that] I rescued this historically significant documentary.” Not everyone who uses private trackers shares Jane’s amateur-archivist zeal. item.dc:creator: Janko Roettgers
item.content:encoded: When Jane first heard about Memory and Imagination , a rare 1990s documentary about the Library of Congress, she was intrigued. But the Canadian writer in her 30s couldn’t find the movie anywhere — not on streaming services, not on YouTube, not on pirate sites — and her intrigue turned into obsession. Worried it might become a lost film , Jane decided to scour auction sites, search every library catalog she could think of, and even enlist some of her online acquaintances to find a copy. Her plan was to “share it with other people to help ensure it would be preserved into the future,” as she puts it. Jane knew the perfect tool for the task: a private torrent tracker. “I am ethically conflicted about piracy. I often feel guilty about it.” Private trackers are essentially the speakeasies of the online piracy world. Promoted primarily by word of mouth, they rely on secrecy, exclusivity, and strict community rules to shield everything that’s going on behind closed doors from the public’s prying eyes. What unites these communities is that they all use BitTorrent to trade media among like-minded file sharers. But their focuses range widely, from general-purpose trackers with catalogs so broad that they make Netflix look like a niche service to the many specialized communities for categories like Chinese movies, motorsports, visual effects tools, e-learning courses, and Japanese porn. There’s even a private tracker just for Frank Zappa music. Private trackers are known for massive and meticulously organized catalogs, which they owe to users like Jane, who, like every other pirate I talked to for this story, opted to be identified by a pseudonym due to the terabytes of copyrighted data they’ve been sharing. These are people willing to go the extra mile to find long-forgotten movies, rare concert recordings, or out-of-print books. “Many private tracker users are fully consumed with archive fever,” she says. At first, Jane had no luck finding a physical copy of that elusive documentary, which includes interviews with Steve Jobs and Julia Child. Nobody was selling it on eBay. Her local public library didn’t have it. Neither did any other public library in North America. And when she finally located a DVD that was available to the public, it was in the Bibliotheca Alexandrina — Egypt’s modern-day re-creation of the ancient library that’s long been synonymous with lost media. “That bowled me over,” Jane says. “This obscure movie I’m looking for is only available in the Library of Alexandria!” Eventually, Jane found Memory and Imagination for sale on a small online marketplace for historical media. Jane instantly bought a copy and uploaded it. “It looked like a digital rip of a severely degraded VHS tape,” she says. “I was still over the moon [that] I rescued this historically significant documentary.” Not everyone who uses private trackers shares Jane’s amateur-archivist zeal. Some are simply in it for easy access to pirated movies, TV shows, or other forms of entertainment. “My goal initially was to have a better source for video games,” says Odel, a West Coast-based college student. “I quickly found out that [private trackers] could replace everything else.” Others join trackers in search of a community of like-minded cinephiles or music fans. And as they immerse themselves in a world of illicit media trading that’s largely shielded from public view, many of them seem to catch a peculiar kind of bug. “There aren’t many closed doors on the internet.” They painstakingly work their way up the ranks in the trackers they’ve joined and then use their freshly earned social capital to get access to even more exclusive sites, where the same rat race starts all over again. “Exclusivity definitely plays a part,” says Maysay, a private tracker user from Pakistan. “You want to get into those more exclusive ‘elite’ trackers at some point just for the sake of it.” “There is definitely a constant quest to level up,” says Jane, who maintains active accounts on 14 private trackers. Among the people I talked to for this story, that’s actually a small number. Some private tracker users maintain dozens of accounts, download terabytes of data, share thousands of torrents at a time, embark on obsessive quests to get their hands on long-lost media, and use automated apps and tools that make everyday piracy seem like child’s play. In a world where streaming services offer access to countless movies and TV shows for little more than your credit card number, private trackers can seem a bit like a throwback. A nod to a different time, when legal options didn’t really exist and file sharing happened in private chat rooms or on password-protected FTP servers. “There aren’t many closed doors on the internet,” says Jane, who became interested in joining private trackers after hearing about them from friends. Jane quickly realized that she couldn’t just sign up for the latest and greatest movie trackers, which were only open to vetted users with a history of good behavior on other servers. So she devised a plan to join a more lenient private tracker for audiobooks first and work her way up from there. Users who fall below certain metrics often find their download privileges curtailed, and especially egregious offenses result in instant bans. Even getting access to that first server came with some hurdles. Private tracker websites rarely have freely accessible sign-up forms. Some only open their doors to new users every few weeks or months, while others use special vetting processes to make sure applicants are a good fit. Sometimes this means that applicants are required to prove they’re in good standing on other trackers. Sometimes they need to take screenshots of their personal media collections to show they’re actually interested in what the tracker they’re applying to is all about. And sometimes there are even actual interviews applicants have to ace before getting their accounts. The long-defunct private music tracker What.CD used to quiz applicants about audio formats and MP3 encoder settings, and even published a study guide of sorts to help them prepare for it. And Jane’s very first private tracker required her to first join an IRC chatroom, where admins quizzed her about the server’s rules. “It was so stressful! It felt like a job interview,” she says. Not every private tracker has these kinds of interviews, but like Jane’s first server, most are big on rules. Users are generally required to keep up a certain upload-to-download ratio, with many sites demanding that they contribute as much bandwidth as they consume. (The exact rules and requirements vary, and many trackers also offer some “freeleech” content — files that can be downloaded without negatively impacting a user’s ratio.) Quickly downloading a file without sharing it is also frowned upon, as is the unvetted distribution of invites to outsiders. Users who fall below certain metrics often find their download privileges curtailed, and especially egregious offenses result in instant bans. “Invite selling is considered to be a major breach of security,” says Odel. Doing so will not only get you kicked from a server, it will also tarnish your reputation elsewhere. “Staff of the tracker you did it on will typically communicate with the staff of some other trackers, which can result in you getting banned from those places as well,” Odel explains. If you do follow the rules and share generously, you have a chance to work your way up the ranks, which then opens the doors to other trackers. That alone, and the requirement to keep up a healthy upload-to-download ratio, can lead to people downloading and then redistributing (also known as “seeding” in tracker lingo) files just to maintain their stats. “Some places will require you to seed [a certain amount of] terabytes before you get access to a certain rank,” says Odel. “This can result in a lot of downloading of stuff I wouldn’t ever consume otherwise, just to pump

item.title: CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars
item.description: 6 Min Read CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars The CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2 crew egress from their simulated Mars habitat, completing their mission on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credits: NASA/James Blair After 378 days without windows, the sounds of the outside world, or real-time calls with family and friends, four research volunteers stepped out of NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, completing the agency’s second yearlong Mars surface simulation. Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer, and Matthew Montgomery entered the roughly 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 19, 2025, for CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2. The crew participated in simulated Marswalks, robotic operations, habitat maintenance, exercise, and crop cultivation. “Their work means more than completing a mission,” said Johnson Director Vanessa Wyche. “It is about preparing for the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth, gathering the knowledge we need to protect crew health and performance, and paving the way for future missions to the Moon and, one day, Mars.” Family, friends, and colleagues welcome the CHAPEA Mission 2 crew as they exit the building housing the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, 2026. NASA/James Blair NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway put the crew’s time in isolation into perspective: While they were inside the habitat, he completed a 237-day mission aboard the space station and returned to Earth. During that same period, the Artemis II astronauts traveled around the Moon and set the record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. NASA also celebrated 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the International Space Station on Nov. 2, 2025. “The reality of what you guys did here required immense physiological and psychological strength, teamwork, and human grit,” Hathaway said. Supported by researchers and ground teams across the agency, the CHAPEA crew collected health and performance data while navigating limited resources and communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way. Ross Elder: Commander and Test Pilot Ross Elder, CHAPEA Mission 2 commander, prepares for a simulated Marswalk in the habitat’s airlock. Elder brought a U.S. Air Force experimental test pilot’s approach to leading the crew. He found simulated Marswalks and robotic exploration “uncannily similar” to operating as part of a flight. From inside the habitat, crew members remotely operated a drone and a rover to survey terrain and identify or collect rock samples. item.content:encoded: 6 Min Read CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars The CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2 crew egress from their simulated Mars habitat, completing their mission on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credits: NASA/James Blair After 378 days without windows, the sounds of the outside world, or real-time calls with family and friends, four research volunteers stepped out of NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, completing the agency’s second yearlong Mars surface simulation. Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer, and Matthew Montgomery entered the roughly 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 19, 2025, for CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2. The crew participated in simulated Marswalks, robotic operations, habitat maintenance, exercise, and crop cultivation. “Their work means more than completing a mission,” said Johnson Director Vanessa Wyche. “It is about preparing for the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth, gathering the knowledge we need to protect crew health and performance, and paving the way for future missions to the Moon and, one day, Mars.” Family, friends, and colleagues welcome the CHAPEA Mission 2 crew as they exit the building housing the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, 2026. NASA/James Blair NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway put the crew’s time in isolation into perspective: While they were inside the habitat, he completed a 237-day mission aboard the space station and returned to Earth. During that same period, the Artemis II astronauts traveled around the Moon and set the record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. NASA also celebrated 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the International Space Station on Nov. 2, 2025. “The reality of what you guys did here required immense physiological and psychological strength, teamwork, and human grit,” Hathaway said. Supported by researchers and ground teams across the agency, the CHAPEA crew collected health and performance data while navigating limited resources and communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way. Ross Elder: Commander and Test Pilot Ross Elder, CHAPEA Mission 2 commander, prepares for a simulated Marswalk in the habitat’s airlock. Elder brought a U.S. Air Force experimental test pilot’s approach to leading the crew. He found simulated Marswalks and robotic exploration “uncannily similar” to operating as part of a flight. From inside the habitat, crew members remotely operated a drone and a rover to survey terrain and identify or collect rock samples. The demanding Marswalk schedule also sharpened his understanding of the physical preparation future explorers will need. Preparing suits, completing airlock procedures, and making long traverses took time and stamina. He emphasized nutrition, exercise, and rest as essential to sustaining that pace. His steadfast leadership and mission focus drew praise at egress for keeping the team motivated and improving. For Elder, seeing his crewmates combine their strengths was a highlight of the mission. “The real magic has been the privilege and pleasure of seeing everyone come together, with the makings of one of the finest teams I’ve ever been a part of,” Elder said. Ellen Ellis: Medical Officer and Tactical Thinker Ellen Ellis, CHAPEA Mission 2 medical officer, exercises on a stationary bike inside the habitat. Ellis, a U.S. Space Force officer with experience at the National Reconnaissance Office, brought a background in military operations and systems engineering. As medical officer, she helped organize biological sample collections and prepare supplies for the crew’s health research. As procedures became familiar, she emphasized the discipline needed to follow every step carefully. She also enjoyed solving problems with the tools available. “There is a kind of tactical creativity that I find energizing,” she said. Contributing to human spaceflight research helped sustain her motivation. So did the relationships with her crewmates. “It would be difficult to convince someone who has never lived in isolation that most days, I don’t feel isolated. I have three teammates that I rely on every day to get through the mission.” She also credited exercise, behavioral health, nutrition, and medical specialists for their coordinated support throughout the mission. “When I look back on the mission, the most salient point I’ve learned is that a future Mars crew requires a highly integrated ground team,” Ellis said. James Spicer: Flight Engineer and Systems Specialist James Spicer, CHAPEA Mission 2 flight engineer, conducts a maintenance activity outside the habitat during a simulated Marswalk. Spicer brought experience in satellite communications and spacecraft development to the habitat’s maintenance work. At egress, he was thanked for keeping its systems running smoothly and described as the “flight engineer extraordinaire and resident data scientist.” He compared the year to living aboard a submarine or boat, where limited supplies and space shaped daily decisions. The crew tracked consumables from dish soap to respirator filters and carefully managed food and water. The crew had access to resources that provided news, and Spicer was surprised by how little he missed constant news and social media updates. The break from distractions helped him focus on the mission. Inside the habitat, stories and jokes around the kitchen table brought laughter to demanding days. He told his crewmates they had made the year “not a chore, but a joy.” “We’re inspired every day knowing that the data we’re generating is informing Martian mission planning and increasing the safety, health, performance, and comfort of future Martian crews,” he said. Matthew Montgomery: Science Officer and Versatile Engineer Matthew Montgomery, CHAPEA Mission 2 science officer, displays vegetables harvested from the habitat’s hydroponic crop system. Montgomery brought experience in hardware engineering, robotics, technology startups, and independent films. At egress, he was described as the “Swiss Army knife of crewmates” for his technical knowledge and problem-solving skills. He helped crewmates identify rock samples collected during simulated Marswalks and set up the habitat’s 3D printing capabilities. His background in indoor agriculture also carried into a seed-germination experiment that used a control and simulated Martian soil. Maintaining a consistent data set remained a priority. Montgomery learned to investigate anything that gave him pause, describing instances when speaking up helped identify concerns with equipment, safety, and data quality. He also learned to give himself more grace when an outcome fell short. At egress, he credited the crew’s different perspectives with producing solutions stronger than any member could have developed alone. “It’s really the people that make exploration possible,” he said. Looking Toward Mars The CHAPEA Mission 2 crew celebrates after stepping outdoors for the first time in 378 days on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center. NASA/James Blair Two weeks of post-mission evaluations and debriefs will help researchers interpret the crew’s data alongside their experiences. The study builds on the first CHAPEA mission, which concluded July 6, 2024. Grace Douglas, CHAPEA’s principal investigator, said the research will help NASA weigh human health and performance risks against resources, including crew time, communication capacity, and food and water system designs. She also noted that many resource challenges facing space explorers mirror problems on Earth. item.title: Yes, it runs 'Doom': Satellite plays iconic game in world's 1st demonstration of orbital voice control
item.description: null A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space. Playing a first-person shooter from 1993 was obviously not in the design plan for the PRETTY cubesat , which is run by a consortium including the European Space Agency (ESA). But the pioneering voice command opens up new worlds for satellite work, the team says. "Someone in distress at sea or in a remote area could transmit 'mayday' or "help" on a radio," stated Estonia's Tanagra Space, which supplied the software for the feat. The hope is one day, a satellite could use transcription and AI to alert rescue services for assisting folks in remote zones. The call to play Doom, thankfully, had no other urgency than curiosity — and teamwork, fueled by pizza. OPS-SAT Space Lab managed the experiment on behalf of ESA. Radio amateurs then made six unsuccessful attempts during passes over Poland and Norway, between April and July. The seventh finally reached success under the Oslo Group of the Norwegian Radio Relay League. "We are radio amateurs, with the emphasis on amateurs. Satellite work was not something our club did, and we had no budget for it," representative Eskil Hadland, call sign LB6AJ, said in the Tangara statement. "So we borrowed a line wrongly credited to Pippi Longstocking: 'I have never tried that before, so I should definitely be able to do that.'" The Norwegians spent 59 days and about 7200 NOK or $775 (pizza included) to reach PRETTY, helping make changes to the satellite software to pick up a voice. For example, a raw recording of an attempt on July 3, retransmitted to Earth, showed the spoken words to space were unrecognizable. Further work revealed the satellite's receiver channel was too wide to pick up the voice signal, leading to a fix to narrow the channel. The historic voice command on July 27— in part, "PRETTY play Doom Doom Doom"— came from a rooftop in Oslo, and was spoken at night by Jon Bergli Heier (LB9BJ). PRETTY picked up the transmission, transcribed the command using on-board voice recognition, and then — just like a typical evening gamer—opened up Doom for a play session. A member of the LB9BJ team speaks the command that activated Doom on the OPS-SAT PRETTY satellite while on a rooftop in Oslo, Norway during an evening pass of the spacecraft on July 27, 2026. (Image credit: Truls Johansen (LA7IJ), LA4O) This was no multiplayer gaming situation, but the satellite did create a report of its demon-slaying skills — and its ability to interpret the command. For example, PRETTY generated a "postcard" including a frame of the gameplay, a transcription, and signal diagnostics. The satellite also transmitted its recording of Hadland's command. As anybody who uses voice-recognition software knows, there are challenges in transcriptions: nobody speaks in exactly the same way, and aspects such as accent or background noise can lead to misinterpretations. The satellite also had to contend with Doppler shift

item.content:encoded: null A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space. Playing a first-person shooter from 1993 was obviously not in the design plan for the PRETTY cubesat , which is run by a consortium including the European Space Agency (ESA). But the pioneering voice command opens up new worlds for satellite work, the team says. "Someone in distress at sea or in a remote area could transmit 'mayday' or "help" on a radio," stated Estonia's Tanagra Space, which supplied the software for the feat. The hope is one day, a satellite could use transcription and AI to alert rescue services for assisting folks in remote zones. The call to play Doom, thankfully, had no other urgency than curiosity — and teamwork, fueled by pizza. OPS-SAT Space Lab managed the experiment on behalf of ESA. Radio amateurs then made six unsuccessful attempts during passes over Poland and Norway, between April and July. The seventh finally reached success under the Oslo Group of the Norwegian Radio Relay League. "We are radio amateurs, with the emphasis on amateurs. Satellite work was not something our club did, and we had no budget for it," representative Eskil Hadland, call sign LB6AJ, said in the Tangara statement. "So we borrowed a line wrongly credited to Pippi Longstocking: 'I have never tried that before, so I should definitely be able to do that.'" The Norwegians spent 59 days and about 7200 NOK or $775 (pizza included) to reach PRETTY, helping make changes to the satellite software to pick up a voice. For example, a raw recording of an attempt on July 3, retransmitted to Earth, showed the spoken words to space were unrecognizable. Further work revealed the satellite's receiver channel was too wide to pick up the voice signal, leading to a fix to narrow the channel. The historic voice command on July 27— in part, "PRETTY play Doom Doom Doom"— came from a rooftop in Oslo, and was spoken at night by Jon Bergli Heier (LB9BJ). PRETTY picked up the transmission, transcribed the command using on-board voice recognition, and then — just like a typical evening gamer—opened up Doom for a play session. A member of the LB9BJ team speaks the command that activated Doom on the OPS-SAT PRETTY satellite while on a rooftop in Oslo, Norway during an evening pass of the spacecraft on July 27, 2026. (Image credit: Truls Johansen (LA7IJ), LA4O) This was no multiplayer gaming situation, but the satellite did create a report of its demon-slaying skills — and its ability to interpret the command. For example, PRETTY generated a "postcard" including a frame of the gameplay, a transcription, and signal diagnostics. The satellite also transmitted its recording of Hadland's command. As anybody who uses voice-recognition software knows, there are challenges in transcriptions: nobody speaks in exactly the same way, and aspects such as accent or background noise can lead to misinterpretations. The satellite also had to contend with Doppler shift, and with an antenna not designed to relay voices to space. But the transmission clearly worked, powered by open-source tools including GNU Radio (which handled the signal processing) and Sherpa-ONNX (speech recognition). The hope is that future spacecraft could one day adapt this approach to radio frequencies for other ideas outside of spoken words. For example, perhaps deep-space radio signals could be detected via satellite, with an AI on board sending the most relevant data to operators after analyzing the work. For now, however, the Norwegian radio operators are basking in the success: "Our tiny ground station shouted at an ESA spacecraft, and was heard," Hadland said.

item.title: From “Behind The Scenes” to “Call of My Life”: 5 All-Time Highest-Grossing Nollywood Movies
item.description: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Nigerian cinema has witnessed an unprecedented commercial evolution over recent years, with local box office totals soaring past figures once considered unthinkable. From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. Here is a look at the five highest-grossing Nollywood blockbusters in history that have continually redefined theatrical success, shattered industry records, and set historic commercial benchmarks across Nigerian cinemas. A Tribe Called Judah (2023) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.40 Billion When this family heist drama landed in Nigerian cinemas on 15 December 2023, few anticipated just how dramatically it would reset the financial ceiling for homegrown features. Directed by Funke Akindele and Tobi Makinde for the Funke Ayotunde Akindele Network (FAAN), the story follows Jedidah Judah—played by Akindele herself—and her five sons from different fathers as they scheme to rob a luxury furniture shop to fund their mother’s life-saving medical care. Supported by a stellar lineup including Timini Egbuson , Jide Kene Achufusi , Uzee Usman , Tobi Makinde , Olumide Oworu , Nse Ikpe Etim , and Genoveva Umeh , the narrative struck a deep chord across multiplexes. By the end of its theatrical run, the project had earned over ₦1.40 Billion, making history as the very first Nollywood title to surpass the ₦1 Billion domestic milestone and cementing Funke Akindele’s status as a formidable box office power. A Tribe Called Judah poster celebrating its historic ₦1 Billion box office milestone. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Nigerian cinema has witnessed an unprecedented commercial evolution over recent years, with local box office totals soaring past figures once considered unthinkable. From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. Here is a look at the five highest-grossing Nollywood blockbusters in history that have continually redefined theatrical success, shattered industry records, and set historic commercial benchmarks across Nigerian cinemas. A Tribe Called Judah (2023) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.40 Billion When this family heist drama landed in Nigerian cinemas on 15 December 2023, few anticipated just how dramatically it would reset the financial ceiling for homegrown features. Directed by Funke Akindele and Tobi Makinde for the Funke Ayotunde Akindele Network (FAAN), the story follows Jedidah Judah—played by Akindele herself—and her five sons from different fathers as they scheme to rob a luxury furniture shop to fund their mother’s life-saving medical care. Supported by a stellar lineup including Timini Egbuson , Jide Kene Achufusi , Uzee Usman , Tobi Makinde , Olumide Oworu , Nse Ikpe Etim , and Genoveva Umeh , the narrative struck a deep chord across multiplexes. By the end of its theatrical run, the project had earned over ₦1.40 Billion, making history as the very first Nollywood title to surpass the ₦1 Billion domestic milestone and cementing Funke Akindele’s status as a formidable box office power. A Tribe Called Judah poster celebrating its historic ₦1 Billion box office milestone. Photo Credit: Filmone/Instagram Everybody Loves Jenifa (2024) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.88 Billion FAAN Studios returned to the festive release window on 13 December 2024 with a comedy-drama co-directed by Funke Akindele and Tunde Olaoye. Centred on the enduring popularity of the lead character, the narrative charts Jenifa’s latest misadventures across global settings, societal expectations, and personal choices, bolstered by on-screen performances from Falz , Layi Wasabi , Patience Ozokwor , and Stan Nze . Building rapidly on its festive debut, the feature went on to generate ₦1.88 Billion in local ticket sales. The milestone surpassed Akindele’s previous commercial record and established an extraordinary streak of back-to-back record-breaking theatrical hits. Funke Akindele and Falz on the ₦1 Billion milestone poster for Everybody Loves Jenifa. Photo Credit: Funke Akindele/Instagram Oversabi Aunty (2025) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.17 Billion Toyin Abraham made her big-screen directorial debut with this comedy-drama from Toyin Abraham Films, which opened in cinemas nationwide on 19 December 2025. The plot introduces Toun, an overzealous church usher and self-styled neighborhood moral authority whose relentless meddling in family and community affairs triggers widespread hilarity and domestic chaos. Abraham leads an ensemble cast alongside Mike Ezuruonye , Lateef Adedimeji , Mercy Aigbe , Odunlade Adekola , Femi Adebayo , and Efe Irele . Finishing its run at ₦1.17 Billion , the project set a career-high theatrical record for Toyin Abraham, making her the second filmmaker in Nigerian cinema history to steer a feature past the ₦1 Billion threshold. Toyin Abraham and cast members on the ₦1 Billion milestone poster for Oversabi Aunty. Photo Credit: Filmone/Instagram Behind The Scenes (2025) — Domestic Box Office: ₦2.76 Billion Arriving in cinemas on 12 December 2025, this festive satire from FAAN Studios, co-directed by Funke Akindele and Tunde Olaoye, takes an unfiltered look at the ambition and internal friction governing the film industry. The story centers on Aderonke Fernandez—portrayed by Scarlet Gomez —a wealthy real estate mogul whose generosity is continually exploited by her extended family until she decides enough is enough. Akindele stars alongside an expansive cast featuring Tobi Bakre , Uzor Arukwe , Uche Montana , Destiny Etiko , and Ini Dima-Okojie . The release made immediate history by crossing half a billion Naira within twelve days, before going on to break every existing West African box office record. It became the first Nollywood movie to cross the ₦2 Billion barrier, topping all-time theatrical rankings with a total gross of ₦2.76 Billion. Funke Akindele on the milestone poster for Behind The Scenes after crossing ₦2 Billion. Call of My Life (2026) — Domestic Box Office: ₦902 Million Directed by Dammy Twitch , written by Uzoamaka Power , and produced by Blessing Uzzi under Bluhouse Studios, this romantic comedy was released in cinemas on 15 May 2026. The story follows Soluchi, a heartbroken call-centre agent whose life takes a sharp turn when a routine customer call with a charming presenter named Eli rekindles her belief in love. The cast stars Uzoamaka Power alongside Andrew Yaw Bunting , Beverly Osu , Zubby Michael , Broda Shaggi , Nkem Owoh , and Patience Ozokwor . The project completely redefined non-festive box office expectations by becoming the highest-grossing mid-year release outside the traditional December festive window. It crossed the ₦600 Million mark faster than any non-December release in Nollywood history, finishing its theatrical run at ₦902 Million and outperforming legacy blockbusters like Battle on Buka Street and Omo Ghetto: The Saga . The stars of Call of My Life gather for the film’s Lagos premiere. Featured from left are Andrew Bunting, Uzoamaka Power, veteran actor Nkem Owoh, producer Blessing Uzzi, director Dammy Twitch, and actress Beverly Osu. item.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
item.description: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference. The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement. The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation. Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation. Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient. Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations. A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work programme” would be included in the agenda. African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops. The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items. A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31. Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. – Fossil fuel fight – Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference. The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement. The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation. Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation. Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient. Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations. A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work programme” would be included in the agenda. African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops. The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items. A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31. Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. – Fossil fuel fight – Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work. The two sides have celebrated their cooperation so far, with COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey’s environment minister, and Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen raising their clasped hands above their heads to applause during the opening ceremony. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. “We know that delay carries one of the heaviest costs in climate action,” Kurum said. Turkey is inviting countries to join a voluntary “electrification” pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. – ‘Clean’ electrification? – But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. COP30 ended with a deal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels after oil-producing countries opposed the language. Instead, Brazil produced a voluntary “roadmap” with proposals for phasing out fossil fuels that each country can tailor to their circumstances. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who will be among leaders addressing COP31 later this week, was due to arrive late Monday, fresh from a re-election win that activists hailed as a victory for climate change. But climate diplomacy is still missing a major player as climate-sceptic US President Donald Trump has not sent officials to COP31. A US congressional delegation, however, will come to Antalya, with Democrats beaming after last week’s historic US midterm election win. item.title: AI Slop FM radio experiment puts machines on trial, one dodgy tune at a time
item.description: A Welsh music enthusiast has built an internet radio station that plays AI-generated tunes alongside human-made tracks without telling listeners which is which, to find out whether listeners really hate AI music or just the idea of it. AI Slop FM is the creation of Mike Chaffin, who built and runs the station single-handedly from Ammanford, Carmarthenshire. By stripping away artist names, cover art, and any mention of AI, Chaffin hopes to find out what listeners really think when they have nothing but the music to go on. The free 24/7 station asks listeners to rate tracks from S to E, tag how the music makes them feel, and leave written feedback. The most popular submissions will eventually make it into a weekly chart called the Slop 40, giving creators something that can be hard to come by in the age of streaming: an actual audience. Anyone can submit a track, including human musicians, although Chaffin has already discovered that not all of them are particularly keen on the idea. He told The Register that he had floated the idea to an unsigned musician friend who had sold around 600 albums, but was met with a rather nervous response. "Wh, wh, why would I want to do that?" the musician reportedly asked, according to Chaffin, who said he had never heard his friend stutter before. "It seems that there is a deep rooted fear of AI music in the industry," Chaffin said. The station is still in beta, with Chaffin waiting for enough submissions to fill its schedule across different genres before opening it fully. He's already been pleasantly surprised by the quality of the music submitted, although he still listens to every track to make sure nobody is trying to pass off Bohemian Rhapsody as their own work. Among the early offerings are what Chaffin describes as a developing genre of slightly rude protest songs about HR departments, along with an operatic epic about a blocked toilet. "Some of which are hilarious," he said of the HR songs. As for the toilet opera, it "runs through my head about once a day, whether I like it or not." Chaffin believes the sheer volume of music uploaded to streaming platforms means plenty of perfectly decent tracks never find an audience, whether a person or a machine made them. He hopes AI Slop FM will give some of those overlooked creations a chance to be heard. "You don't have to have published your creations to upload. Just to own the rights," he explained. Tracks that don't make the Slop 40 could still get another outing, with plans for genre-specific stations offering unsuccessful submissions a second chance. The bigger question is what happens when listeners start rating AI-generated music more highly than the human competition, but Chaffin isn't particularly worried about that. "If the machines win then their creators clearly deserve to be heard, deserve an audience. If the musicians win, then that's reassuring for them."
